Barleybrew has stationed himself at the tavern in Lakeshire, right on the front lines of Redridge's struggle against encroaching gnolls and Blackrock orcs. Those who track him down find a boastful dwarf with a hearty drink in hand, ready to size up any challenger who claims to possess real fighting spirit. For warriors seeking to prove themselves beyond the safe cobbled streets of the capital, his trial marks an initiation into harsher frontier battles.

quest:1716.text: Devourer of Souls. Devourer of Souls is a pivotal rite of passage for Alliance warlocks dispatched from Stormwind to learn the summoning of a succubus. Directed by Gakin the Darkbinder, initiates must trek halfway across the world into the hazardous wildlands of the Barrens to seek counsel from Takar the Seer. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder instructs promising warlocks on their next major summons: the succubus. Described as a devourer of souls, a destroyer of hearts, and a dominator of minds, this demonic entity cannot be summoned blindly into Azeroth. It requires a potent lure, specifically an object tied to pure love, to tease it forth from the Twisting Nether so that the practitioner may defeat and bind it. Procuring such a token demands wisdom that Stormwind's covens cannot provide locally. To track down the required catalyst, Gakin sends his pupils across the Great Sea to Kalimdor. Deep in the arid expanse of the Barrens, near the Horde settlement of Camp Taurajo, sits Takar the Seer. For an Alliance warlock, reaching Takar requires braving wilderness heavily patrolled by hostile centaur, quilboar, and Horde warriors, serving as an unstated test of survival before the summoner can even begin preparing the ritual.

quest:1717.text: Gakin's Summons. A summons delivered to promising Alliance warlocks in Ironforge, directing them south to Stormwind. Gakin the Darkbinder awaits beneath the city's Mage Quarter to oversee their advancement into commanding greater fiends. Demonology remains a practice conducted entirely in shadows across Alliance lands. In Ironforge, Lago Blackwrench quietly keeps tabs on wandering practitioners on behalf of the brotherhood in Stormwind. When a warlock shows sufficient mastery over their initial minions, word travels quickly. Lago passes along the directive: drop whatever business keeps you in the snowy mountains of Khaz Modan and report south without delay. Deep beneath the cobblestones of Stormwind's Mage Quarter, beneath the tavern known as The Slaughtered Lamb, Gakin the Darkbinder coordinates the development of the city's warlocks. Gakin views every capable student as a valuable, hazardous investment. Receiving his summons marks the threshold of true demonic binding, beginning the trials required to subjugate a succubus from the Twisting Nether.

quest:1738.text: Heartswood. Heartswood is an Alliance warlock quest that sends practitioners deep into Ashenvale to recover the branch of an ancient, tragic tree. Sent by the hermit Takar the Seer on behalf of Gakin the Darkbinder, warlocks seek this romantic relic as a potent bait to lure and subjugate a succubus in Stormwind. According to Takar the Seer, the Heartswood tree sprang from the spot where two night elf lovers, Anathera and Latherion, fell together during the War of the Ancients ten thousand years ago. Nourished by their final breaths and eternal devotion, the tree grew as a pure emblem of undying romance. To mortal senses it is a sacred tragic monument, but to practitioners of the dark arts, concentrated emotional energy makes potent magical fuel. Succubi feed upon mortal passions, desire, and emotional torment. Takar realizes that ordinary temptations pale in comparison to an artifact suffused with thousands of years of pure, undying devotion. A piece of the Heartswood provides Gakin the Darkbinder with the exact catalyst required to bait one of these cunning demons across the Nether into the summoning circle in Stormwind's Mage Quarter.

quest:1739.text: The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation ritual for Alliance warlocks seeking to command a succubus in Stormwind. Using the enchanted core obtained from the Heartswood, the practitioner enters the summoning circle beneath The Slaughtered Lamb to drag forth and physically overpower the demon. Once defeated, the demon's will is chained, binding its servitude to the summoner. Hidden beneath the floorboards of The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter lies a cavernous crypt dedicated to forbidden arts. Far from the watchful eyes of the city watch and the Cathedral of Light, the city's covert warlock enclave conducts its most dangerous rituals here. Summoning circles etched into stone channel the raw forces of the Nether, allowing ambitious initiates to pierce the veil between worlds. Summoning a succubus requires far more than merely chanting incantations. A warlock must bring a focus—in this case, the prepared Heartswood Core—and cast a ritual of breach at the circle. Succubi are known to corrupt, seduce, and overwhelm even fortified minds. To establish absolute mastery, the summoner must cut the beast down in single combat, banishing its physical form back to the Twisting Nether while securing its true tether.

quest:1793.text: The Tome of Valor. The Tome of Valor is a foundational trial for Alliance paladins coming into their own. Directed by paladin mentors in Stormwind and Ironforge, initiates are challenged to prove that their courage and devotion to protecting the innocent match their martial prowess. To wield the Holy Light in battle requires more than heavy armor and martial discipline. As young paladins reach greater heights in their training, instructors in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries demand proof of their inner resolve. The lessons of the Tome of Valor test an initiate's readiness to confront terrifying evils—from dragons to demons—without faltering or abandoning those who cannot defend themselves. Bravery under mortal threat is considered as essential to a holy warrior as their weapon and shield. Through the trials laid out in the Tome of Valor, paladins learn that raw strength is hollow without an unwavering vow to shelter the helpless. Facing genuine peril ensures that when darkness falls upon the Alliance, its defenders will stand firm rather than break.

quest:1824.text: Trial at the Field of Giants. Trial at the Field of Giants is a warrior rites quest issued by Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo. As part of their training, martial aspirants are dispatched south into the swarming mounds of the Field of Giants to slay alien insectoid invaders. Candidates must harvest several still-twitching antennae and rush them back before the biological proof goes dormant. Warrior trainers among the Horde rarely accept mere martial competence without testing fortitude and urgency. Ruga Ragetotem challenges growing warriors at Camp Taurajo to prove themselves against an unfamiliar adversary. Aspirants are not just ordered to slay the encroaching creatures; they must sever fresh antennae and return to Taurajo within half an hour before the harvested tissue ceases twitching, demanding rapid navigation of the southern Barrens. The targets of the trial are the silithid hives burgeoning in the Field of Giants, nestled beneath massive fossilized ribcages. These crawling, chitinous insects are recent arrivals to the Barrens, disturbing the tauren hunters and shamans who watch the savannas. Ruga notes with dread that their presence bodes ill for Kalimdor, making the extermination test serve a dual purpose: proving a young warrior's combat instincts while gathering intelligence on a looming ecological menace.

quest:1825.text: Speak with Thun'grim. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze, an acclaimed orc blacksmith camping in the Barrens. Having proved themselves through demanding physical trials, warriors are invited to have custom armor forged in recognition of their valor. The quest serves as the crucial bridge connecting general warrior testing with the crafting of Brutal Armor. After proving their mettle against the silithid hives during the Trial at the Field of Giants, Horde warriors earn more than simple praise from Ruga Ragetotem. Word of their endurance and martial prowess quickly reaches Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc smith who maintains a camp perched on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Recognizing a warrior worthy of his craft, Thun'grim sends word that he wishes to fashion them an exceptional suit of battle mail. Thun'grim Firegaze does not forge for ordinary soldiers. For an armorsmith of his reputation, steel must match the spirit of the one who carries it into battle. Reaching his camp signifies that a warrior has advanced past simple militia drills and is ready to undertake the grueling, specialized tasks required to gather rare crafting reagents across Kalimdor.

quest:185.text: Tiger Mastery. At the northern safari camp in Stranglethorn Vale, the hunter Ajeck Rouack offers to train adventurers in the discipline of big cat stalking. She starts newcomers against the younger tigers prowling near the camp to test basic hunting and tracking prowess. Having learned the art of hunting tigers from her father when she was a girl, Ajeck Rouack shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition following Welcome to the Jungle. She insists that tracking and slaying the youngest felines is the essential foundation before any hunter can advance to greater quarry. Young Stranglethorn tigers are often found in the jungle close to the expedition camp. Rouack demands that ten of these beasts be hunted down to prove sufficient skill before she agrees to provide any further training.

quest:186.text: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack escalates her hunting trials. Having seen your early promise with young stalkers, he now sends you into the jungle to fell mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Following your initial success against younger predators, Ajeck Rouack seeks to test your growing skills against more seasoned beasts. She directs you back out into the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale to hunt down ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers before you can pursue even greater challenges.

quest:187.text: Tiger Mastery. Deep in the jungle at Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack raises the stakes of his hunting trials. He demands the death of ten elder Stranglethorn tigers to prove your prowess before the final test. Following the earlier hunts, Ajeck Rouack asks you to pursue ten elder Stranglethorn tigers across the wilds. He considers these beasts both the most elusive to track and the fiercest to overcome. Felling ten of them serves as the prelude to a concluding trial, after which he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

quest:188.text: Tiger Mastery. Ajeck Rouack offers the ultimate challenge in his series of hunts within northern Stranglethorn Vale. After weeks of tracking an elusive beast, he challenges you to seek out the tiger Sin'Dall and bring back her paw. Having completed the earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers, you are offered one last challenge by Ajeck Rouack at Nesingwary's Expedition. The hunting camp has tracked an extraordinarily elusive tiger known as Sin'Dall across the jungle for weeks. Ajeck challenges you to track her down, fell the beast, and claim her paw as indisputable proof.

quest:189.text: Bloodscalp Ears. Kebok in Booty Bay is losing guards and agents to jungle clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe. Worried about climbing expenses and answering to Baron Revilgaz, he offers coin to any adventurer willing to hunt down the trolls and return with proof of the kill. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Kebok faces a serious operational dilemma. The local trolls in Stranglethorn Vale have been killing his agents in the jungle, and he has lost many of his best guards in skirmishes with them. With the casualties mounting, so too are the costs, leaving him frantic over how to explain them to Baron Revilgaz. Rather than allowing the losses to accumulate further, Kebok turns to outside help. He offers monetary compensation to travelers who head into the jungle, cull the Bloodscalp trolls, and bring back fifteen of their severed ears as undeniable confirmation of their demise.

quest:190.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition offers a trial to those seeking to prove their prowess as big-game stalkers in Stranglethorn Vale. To join Hemet's hunting company, adventurers must first demonstrate their basic tracking ability by taking down ten young panthers. Within the wild expanse of northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary has assembled a seasoned band of big-game huntsmen. Sir S. J. Erlgadin tells anyone who wants a part of the hunt that they must first prove themselves an able panther hunter. Before Erlgadin entrusts anyone with greater game, he issues an entry test: finding and slaying ten young panthers. Simply finding the beasts is only half the challenge.

quest:191.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin demands that you prove yourself worthy of the big game hunters at Nesingwary's Expedition. Following your initial cull of younger beasts, he challenges you to track down and slay ten fully grown panthers in the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale. After dispatching the young panthers around the jungle, Sir S. J. Erlgadin asks you to raise your sights. To show that you deserve to keep company with seasoned big game hunters, you are sent out to hunt ten mature panthers, which are far tougher and more dangerous than their younger kin.

quest:192.text: Panther Mastery. Sir S. J. Erlgadin of Nesingwary's Expedition challenges big game hunters to track and bring down the deadliest panthers in Stranglethorn Vale. Following your earlier trials, you must now seek out and slay ten Shadowmaw Panthers. Sir S. J. Erlgadin considers Shadowmaw Panthers to be the most dangerous cats prowling the jungles of Stranglethorn. Proving your mettle as a true stalker requires crawling through the dense underbrush to track down ten of these elusive beasts, whose ferocity makes them far harder to kill than to find.

quest:194.text: Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

quest:195.text: Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

quest:198.text: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek in Booty Bay hires a courier to haul miscellaneous goblin supplies north to Lieutenant Doren's camp. Local troll aggression has halted routine shipments, requiring an outside hand to ensure the goods reach Private Thorsen near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren and his outfit stationed near the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood rely on regular shipments arranged through Krazek. Persistent attacks from local trolls have made standard delivery hazardous, prompting the goblin merchant to contract an independent courier. The package must travel all the way up the jungle road, with Private Thorsen designated to receive it either in their camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

quest:1999.text: Tools of the Trade. Tools of the Trade is an initiation mission for Horde rogues given by Mennet Carkad in the Undercity. Ordered by Lord Varimathras, agents must obtain lockpicking gear and infiltrate Ambermill to recover sensitive Kirin Tor reports detailing Dalaran's current state. Following the interrogation of one of their prisoners, the Deathstalkers learned that vital intelligence concerning the ruins of Dalaran lies hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and the human mages guarding the village guard their communications fiercely. Under the orders of Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad directs promising operatives to bypass Kirin Tor sentries and secure the Dalaran Status Report. Unlike straightforward assassinations, this mission serves as a practical proving ground in infiltration and lockpicking. Operatives are outfitted with specialized thieves' tools from Estelle Gendry before marching into hostile Kirin Tor territory. Cracking the secured chest in Ambermill demonstrates that an operative has progressed beyond raw street brutality into an indispensable espionage asset for the Forsaken.

quest:20.text: Blackrock Menace. Marshal Marris of Lakeshire tasks adventurers with culling the aggressive Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. By seizing their battleworn axes, the town's defenders hope to break the siege tightening around the settlement. Lakeshire finds itself hemmed in on multiple fronts, but none pose so dire a threat as the Blackrock orcs spilling over from the fiery Burning Steppes. Having pushed south into Redridge, these veteran raiders have seized strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps the townspeople effectively penned inside the settlement, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads. Marshal Marris, commander of the beleaguered Lakeshire guard, cannot spare a detachment to assault their positions outright. Instead, he enlists roaming adventurers to bleed the invaders' forward scouts and foot soldiers. By demanding their crude, battleworn axes as proof of death, Marris seeks to thin the invaders' numbers both around Stonewatch to the north and in the rugged pockets of southeastern Redridge.

quest:200.text: Bookie Herod. Lieutenant Doren fears a spy among his own men after Kurzen discovered Thorsen's secret. To uncover how the secret slipped out, an investigator must infiltrate Kurzen's Compound and recover the records kept by Kurzen's logistics officer. Following the discovery of Thorsen's secret, Lieutenant Doren suspects that a traitor operates within their midst. The intelligence leak threatens their operations, and finding the traitor has become an urgent concern. Thorsen maintained a line of communication directly into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer. Because Herod knows how Kurzen's Compound is run from day to day, Doren believes the officer's written records hold the truth about how the operation was exposed. Reaching Bookie Herod's paperwork requires venturing into Kurzen's Compound. During Doren's time serving under Kurzen, Herod kept his office on the top floor of the compound's lone two-story house. There, among supply requisitions and missives from Colonel Kurzen himself, lie the documents that could trace how the secret was betrayed.

quest:203.text: The Second Rebellion. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks help against the overwhelming forces of Colonel Kurzen. Outnumbered ten to one by a cunning tactician, the rebels must rely on swift, covert strikes to survive. Cutting down Kurzen's jungle fighters is the first step toward relieving the relentless pressure on their refuge. The soldiers at the Rebel Camp face dire odds against Colonel Kurzen. Yohwa explains that the Colonel is a brilliant military tactician whose force outnumbers the rebellion by at least ten to one. Unable to wage an open war of attrition, the rebels have no choice but to adopt the Colonel's own covert tactics, launching quick incursions into his encampment to thin his ranks and escaping before heavy reinforcements can retaliate. To stem the tide, Yohwa asks you to push east into Kurzen's stronghold and eliminate a sizable contingent of his jungle fighters. Thinning out these foot soldiers eases the pressure bearing down on the Rebel Camp.

quest:204.text: Bad Medicine. At the Rebel Camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Sergeant Yohwa seeks to blunt Colonel Kurzen's military advantage by targeting his medical support. The renegades rely on powerful remedies and toxins concocted by their practitioners, leaving the resistance fighters desperate to turn those same concoctions to their own advantage. Colonel Kurzen has bolstered his jungle force with numerous medicine men who heal his forces and poison Yohwa's fighters with venom fern extracts. To turn the tide of the conflict, Sergeant Yohwa directs adventurers into the Kurzen Compound to scavenge those vital supplies. Securing their jungle remedies will help treat wounded fighters at the Rebel Camp, while capturing a sample of their venom fern extract will enable the resistance to study the toxin and manufacture their own cures.

quest:2040.text: Underground Assault. Underground Assault is an Alliance quest offered by Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind City's Dwarven District. Tasked with aiding the displaced gnomes, adventurers venture into the Deadmines to salvage an intact power core from a goblin shredder. This stolen component is destined to power drilling machines intended to spearhead the liberation of Gnomeregan. Following the catastrophic fall of Gnomeregan to the primitive troggs, surviving gnomish tinkerers have been forced into exile across Khaz Modan and Stormwind. Rather than wallowing in defeat, engineers like Shoni the Shilent are already devising mechanical operations to breach their lost home. The primary obstacle is the dense, subterranean rock surrounding the technocratic city, requiring massive tunneling engines known as gyrodrillmatic excavationators. Lacking the necessary localized power grids in human lands, the gnomes have turned their sights to an unlikely and volatile alternative: goblin heavy machinery operating in the criminal underworld. Deep within the twisting shafts of the Deadmines in Westfall, Edwin VanCleef's Defias Brotherhood employs goblin engineers to manufacture war machines, including a fully operational goblin shredder. Shoni directs Alliance operatives to infiltrate this foundry, destroy or dismantle the lumbering automaton, and recover its specialized heart—the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. By commandeering the potent goblin power supply, the exiled gnomes gain the raw mechanical output needed to bore through the subterranean perimeter and launch a counteroffensive to reclaim Gnomeregan.

quest:2078.text: Gyromast's Revenge. Gelkak Gyromast seeks payback against the local murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship along the Darkshore coastline. To carry out his vendetta, the eccentric captain sends adventurers to reactivate his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Stranded upon the misty strands of Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast refuses to accept defeat at the hands of the shore-dwelling murlocs. Having salvaged the pieces needed to fuel his schemes, the eccentric captain sets his sights on complete retaliation against the tribe and their chief. Rather than wading into the surf with cutlass in hand, Gelkak relies on heavy engineering to exact his vengeance, entrusting a winding key to any landlubber brave enough to handle his mechanical subordinate.

quest:2098.text: Gyromast's Retrieval. Shipwrecked on the misty coast of Darkshore, the eccentric gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast seeks aid to restore his mechanical first mate. His vital winding key was shattered upon the rocks and scavenged by the local wildlife and murlocs. Recovering the three pieces is the first step toward getting his crew back in working order. Gelkak Gyromast is an odd sight along the gloomy sands of Darkshore: a gnome pirate stranded far from the typical sea routes of the South Seas. According to Gelkak, his vessel met an unfortunate end just off the coastline after being attacked and sunk by aggressive threshadons. Washing ashore amid the flotsam, he found himself utterly marooned and separated from his trusty crew. Gelkak's most pressing concern is not provisions or gold, but his first mate. Activating and operating this companion requires a specialized key, which shattered into three distinct fragments when Gelkak crashed onto the rocky shoals. Before he could gather the fragments, the indigenous wildlife—scuttling reef crawlers on the beach, towering foreststriders near the woods, and scavengers from the local Greymist murloc tribe—snatched the shiny metal pieces away.

quest:213.text: Hostile Takeover. Gelriz has been muscling out the moguls appointed by the trade princes and now makes a move on the most notorious pirate of all, and Baron Revilgaz will not stand for it. In response, Kebok in Booty Bay directs adventurers to steal strange blue crystals that Venture Company geologists have been finding near Lake Nazferiti. Gelriz has stepped over the line by shoving aside moguls chosen by the trade princes and making a move on the most notorious pirate of all. Baron Revilgaz refuses to permit such insolence, instructing Kebok to handle the intrusion however he sees fit. Kebok's chosen response is outright theft, targeting the strange blue stones that Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing. Venture Company geologists operating around Lake Nazferiti have taken a keen interest in these unusual crystals. Kebok wants eight samples brought back to Booty Bay, unconcerned with how they are acquired so long as they end up in his hands.

quest:215.text: Jungle Secrets. After being rescued from an ambush in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Private Thorsen explains why he re-enlisted with Kurzen's men. He directs you back to the Rebel Camp so his commander can verify his covert intentions. Following his rescue, Private Thorsen admits the scene looks bad and asks to explain. He claims Lieutenant Doren ordered him to re-enlist with Colonel Kurzen's men to gather desperately needed intelligence for the rebellion. What seemed to be an opportunity to infiltrate Kurzen's Compound quickly turned disastrous, forcing Thorsen to refer you directly to Doren at the Rebel Camp for official confirmation while begging for complete discretion.

quest:2282.text: Alther's Mill. Alther's Mill is a pivotal training assignment given to Alliance rogues by Lucius in Lakeshire. Dispatched to the nearby mill with a set of thieves' tools, initiates are tasked with infiltrating an area under Blackrock orc scrutiny to crack a locked chest and retrieve a token of thievery. In Lakeshire, rogue instructors do not bother with abstract lectures when a locked chest can teach the lesson faster. Lucius sends promising operatives northeast along the road to Alther's Mill, equipping them with their first set of thieves' tools. To earn their formal Certificate of Thievery, novices must slip into the abandoned mill, pick open Lucius's personal lockbox, and bring back the token cached within. While Alther's Mill was once an ordinary lumber outpost, it has recently drawn the dangerous attention of the Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. Lucius gleefully treats the encroaching warmongers as an added layer of practical examination. Prowling through enemy-held territory to pick locks undetected is precisely the kind of trial SI:7 expects its agents to survive.

quest:235.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. Issued by Warcaller Gorlach in Orgrimmar, this directive summons budding Horde adventurers northward beyond the Barrens into the ancient forests of Ashenvale. Players are directed to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to participate in the ongoing hunt and reinforce the Horde's expanding frontier. Orgrimmar buzzes with martial fervor, but the young city requires vast amounts of timber, meat, and secure trade routes to sustain its growth. Warcaller Gorlach serves as the voice of the Horde's high command, directing seasoned wanderers and new blood alike toward active campaigns. For warriors coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, the ancient woodlands of Ashenvale represent the next testing ground for both glory and survival. Crossing the northern border of the Barrens brings travelers directly into Ashenvale, where the Horde maintains two primary bastions: Splintertree Post nestled in the eastern woods and Zoram'gar Outpost along the western coast. Senani Thunderheart coordinates operations at Splintertree Post, organizing trackers and hunters to tame the beast-choked canopy and push back against hostile night elven sentinels disputing the Horde's claims.

quest:240.text: Return to Jitters. Return to Jitters concludes Chef Grual's culinary errand in Duskwood. Having prepared his infamous 'crab' cakes using the gooey legs of the local venom web spiders, Grual sends you back to the starving, terrified hermit at Raven Hill. Delivering the meal finally satisfies Jitters' desperate hunger. Duskwood is short on conventional livestock and sea life, leaving Chef Grual at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to improvise with whatever the blighted forest provides. His renowned 'Dusky Crab Cakes' contain no actual crab meat at all, relying instead on gooey legs harvested from the venom web spiders creeping through the wood. Grual considers this resourceful cooking; anyone with a delicate stomach might view it with horror. Jitters spends his days huddled at Raven Hill, utterly consumed by fright and paralyzed by whatever horrors drove him out of the woods. Weak with terror and unable to muster the courage to hunt or forage for himself, his empty stomach only amplifies his distress. Receiving the warm cakes brings a rare moment of relief to the trembling vagrant, who is far too hungry to question what kind of 'crab' Chef Grual used.

quest:2458.text: Deep Cover. Deep Cover is an undercover assignment given to promising Horde rogues by Shenthul in Orgrimmar. The mission dispatches the operative to the Venture Company drilling grounds at Sludge Fen to establish secret contact with an embedded agent of the Shattered Hand. The Shattered Hand operates as the clandestine intelligence and assassin guild of the Horde, quietly guarding Orgrimmar's interests through ruthlessly practical means. For an entire year, the guild labored to slip an operative into the hierarchy of the rapacious Venture Company. That asset, Taskmaster Fizzule, managed to ingratiate himself into their industrial drilling outpost north of Sludge Fen. Operating deep within mercenary lines leaves no margin for error. Because Fizzule maintains a ruthless persona to satisfy his corporate overseers, any unannounced visitor risks immediate attack. To verify their identity, arriving rogues must fire twin flares from a designated signaling gun within sight of his tower, approach quietly, and perform the secret salute of the Shattered Hand before receiving his report on the Venture Company's escalating schemes.

quest:2460.text: The Shattered Salute. The Shattered Salute is an initiation ritual overseen by Shenthul within the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. By learning this distinct sign of recognition, budding rogues are taught how to safely identify fellow operatives of the Shattered Hand in the field. Within the dark tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow, the Shattered Hand operates as the clandestine intelligence and assassination arm of Thrall's Horde. Given the dangerous and secretive nature of their assignments, operatives cannot rely on overt banners or standard military heraldry. Shenthul instructs newly inducted rogues in the Shattered Salute, a specific gesture meant to serve as an unmistakable, silent signal among allies. Mastering the salute is not merely a ceremonial exercise; it is vital tradecraft. Rogue agents sent into perilous territory or tasked with infiltrating rival factions must verify contacts without alerting bystanders or targets. Shenthul insists that an operative be able to recognize and mirror the gesture effortlessly before entrusting them with covert fieldwork.

quest:2478.text: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. This critical assignment tests a Horde rogue's stealth, thievery, and combat skills against a rogue Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens. Operatives infiltrate an oil tower, assassinate Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, and seize a potent chemical concoction for the Shattered Hand. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company maintains an isolated drilling tower. Under orders from Taskmaster Fizzule, an embedded Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, rogues are instructed to use classic underworld methods rather than outright assault. Fizzule asks rogues to pickpocket a key directly off Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him before mounting an ascent through heavily altered workers and sentries.

quest:2479.text: Hinott's Assistance. Hinott's Assistance is an urgent journey undertaken by Horde rogues suffering from a debilitating tropical toxin. Contracted during an infiltration mission in the Barrens, the affliction requires the specialized expertise of Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill. Seeking his aid promises both a life-saving cure and instruction in the art of concocting deadly poisons. Following the daring infiltration of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen, rogues find themselves afflicted by Zanzil's altered mixture. The poison wreaks havoc on the body, dulling reflexes and threatening life itself. Recognizing the severity of the affliction, rogue trainer Shenthul in Orgrimmar admits that local remedies are inadequate and directs the poisoned operative across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms. The search for a cure leads south through the continent of Lordaeron to the village of Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills. There resides Serge Hinott, an apothecary whose fascination with virulent brews makes him ideally suited to analyze the exotic sample. While ordinary healers recoiled from Zanzil's venom, Hinott treats the deadly compound with professional glee, eager to dissect the foul concoction and instruct worthy rogues in brewing their own venoms.

quest:261.text: Down the Scarlet Path. Brother Anton of the Scarlet Crusade, at Nijel's Point, says his order is at war with the Scourge, an evil that corrupts the people and infects the land. He asks you to prove your allegiance by destroying thirty undead ravagers in the Valley of Bones. Brother Anton speaks bluntly. He says the Scourge must be halted before it swallows the land and pulls the world into darkness, and the Scarlet Crusade has pledged itself to that fight. If you are with them, he wants your courage and allegiance shown by destroying thirty undead ravagers. They are found south of Anton, in the Valley of Bones. Succeed, and the Crusade will welcome you.

quest:276.text: Tramping Paws. Tramping Paws is an Alliance task given by Rethiel the Greenwarden at the Greenwarden's Grove in the Wetlands. Troubled by the surging Mosshide gnoll population near the Gate of Algaz, the bog beast protector tasks adventurers with culling their numbers before their fires and trampling paws ruin the bog. For many years, the Mosshide gnolls inhabited the Wetlands without utterly overwhelming its natural order. Lately, however, their pack numbers have exploded south toward the pass of Dun Algaz. Their heavy boots and pawprints trample rare fen flora, and their crude logging strips vital groves to feed their campsite blazes. Left unchecked, the burgeoning packs threaten to degrade the fragile marsh ecology. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the marsh with an eye for balance rather than civilization. To the Greenwarden, the issue is not that gnolls exist, but that their runaway population outstrips what the Wetlands can support. By driving Mosshide gnolls and mongrels back into manageable numbers, adventurers help preserve the wetlands and earn the reluctant approval of an ancient wilderness guardian.

quest:328.text: The Hidden Key. Tucked away in the binding of Bookie Herod's ledgers is a small brass key alongside notes referencing a secure strongbox. Locating this container deep within the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound may reveal how Private Thorsen was betrayed. Searching through Bookie Herod's ledgers yields no direct mention of Private Thorsen, but it reveals something else: a small brass key concealed inside a book's binding. Scraps among the paperwork make passing mention of a secure strongbox tucked away inside the Stockpile, the cavern complex at the rear of Kurzen's Compound. Opening that container might reveal how Thorsen's cover was blown. Reaching the strongbox requires delving into the cave system behind the compound. Heavy, bronze-bound, and sturdily constructed, the chest sits among stacked crates in the cave.

quest:329.text: The Spy Revealed!. Inside Bookie Herod's strongbox lies a damp piece of parchment detailing the daily routines of Private Thorsen. Bearing only the initial M, this correspondence suggests an informant has embedded themselves among the rebels in northern Stranglethorn Vale. The muddy note is meant for Lieutenant Doren. Opening the strongbox reveals not just valuables, but an itinerary tracking Private Thorsen. The barely legible writing recounts his patrol routes, his companions, and his daily activities around the Rebel Camp, marked only with the signature -M. Such detailed observations could only come from someone living alongside Thorsen, pointing to a traitor within the rebel camp.

quest:330.text: Patrol Schedules. Following the discovery of an incriminating message signed only by an initial, Lieutenant Doren seeks to identify the traitor within the Rebel Camp. By cross-referencing duty rosters, duty records can reveal who shared patrol routes with Private Thorsen during the previous week. The recovered note bears only the initial M, which provides little on its own to expose the conspirator aiding the Kurzen forces. However, the author mentions sharing regular duty paths alongside Private Thorsen throughout the previous week. Lieutenant Doren directs you across the Rebel Camp to speak with Corporal Sethman, the soldier responsible for maintaining duty logs, to identify who walked alongside Thorsen.

quest:331.text: Report to Doren. After obtaining the patrol information, Corporal Sethman directs you back to Lieutenant Doren. Delivering these findings brings crucial military intelligence directly to the rebels' commander in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Corporal Sethman reminds you that Lieutenant Doren wants a direct report on the patrol information. You must bring what you learned back to Doren.

quest:349.text: Stranglethorn Fever. Deep within Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa claims to know how to draw out the beast known as Mokk the Savage. Before communion with the spirits can begin, the witch doctor requires a Gorilla Fang as an offering. Once the ritual commences, defending the troll from agitated jungle beasts is necessary to lure the creature forth. Witch Doctor Unbagwa possesses the ritual knowledge needed to summon Mokk the Savage out of the surrounding jungle. To begin the incantation, the witch doctor demands a Gorilla Fang. Communing with the spirits carries a heavy risk, as the ritual chant draws the attention of other gorilla beasts in the vicinity, demanding protection while the magic does its work.

quest:4021.text: Counterattack!. Following the systematic elimination of their local chieftains in the Barrens, the Kolkar centaur mount a desperate retaliation out of Desolace. An invading force marches directly upon Regthar Deathgate's outpost west of the Crossroads, culminating in a fierce confrontation with Warlord Krom'zar. The campaign against the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens struck deep into their tribal leadership. With Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark dead, the remaining centaur found themselves shattered and without direction. In response to this humiliation, word traveled west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. Rather than scattering into the scrubland, a fresh contingent of hardened Kolkar warriors rallied and crossed into the Barrens, burning for blood and retribution against the fledgling Horde encampments.

quest:442.text: Assault on Fenris Isle. Assault on Fenris Isle is the climactic military directive issued by High Executor Hadrec to eradicate the Scourge stronghold in Silverpine Forest. To break the Lich King's grip upon Lake Lordamere, Forsaken agents are sent to storm Fenris Keep and take the head of the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw. For weeks, Fenris Isle has stood as a poisonous blister in the heart of Lake Lordamere. While the Forsaken secured the western roads and established their presence at the Sepulcher, the Scourge entrenched themselves inside Fenris Keep. Commanded by the powerful necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, this island outpost threatened not only Silverpine Forest but the southern waterways leading toward the Undercity itself. High Executor Hadrec recognizes that the Forsaken will never truly hold Silverpine while a servant of the Lich King conducts vile experiments right off their eastern shores.

quest:455.text: The Algaz Gauntlet. The Algaz Gauntlet is an urgent military mission to fight through Dun Algaz, a critical mountain pass linking Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have entrenched themselves in the tunnels, threatening to sever Ironforge's vital lifeline to Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are tasked with cutting down the orcish vanguard and delivering word of the invasion to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz serves as the solitary overland mountain pass carving through the crags between Loch Modan and the marshy basin of the Wetlands. For the dwarves of Ironforge, this stone corridor is essential for trade, troop movements, and supplies heading to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's primary coastal port in the region. Should the pass fall, Ironforge's connection to the western seas is effectively strangled, leaving isolated outposts cut off from dwarven reinforcements. While remnants of the Dragonmaw clan have long haunted the hills and ruins of the Wetlands following the Second War, their sudden, organized push into Dun Algaz marks an aggressive escalation. Instead of lingering in their marshland enclaves, Dragonmaw scouts and grunts have seized the tunnels and fortified the pass. Mountaineer Rockgar enlists brave Alliance travelers to shatter this blockade by slaying the encroaching orcs and carrying word of the assault directly to Valstag Ironjaw in Menethil Harbor.

quest:463.text: The Greenwarden. "The Greenwarden" is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing travelers deeper into the marshes of the Wetlands. Sent by First Mate Fitzsimmons from Menethil Harbor, adventurers venture northeast into the swamp to seek out a mysterious entity rumored to dwell among the beasts. Around the docks of Menethil Harbor, sailors and wanderers trade breathless stories of a beast lurking out in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons paints the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs, warning gullible seekers that stepping off the dry road means being bitten in two by 'ol' Greenie.' To the dockside folk, anything massive lurking out in the murky waters is just another man-eating hazard of the marsh.

quest:468.text: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Report to Mountaineer Rockgar is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers north from the guard posts of Loch Modan toward Dun Algaz. Mountaineer Kadrell dispatches capable travelers to join Rockgar, who is organizing a vital expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the gateway passage connecting the dwarven homeland to northern territories. Dun Algaz represents the crucial artery between Loch Modan and the marshy expanses of the Wetlands. Built into the northern mountain ridge, the fortified pass has long guaranteed safe passage for trade, messengers, and military detachments moving between Ironforge and Alliance settlements further north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps a close watch on travellers passing through, recruiting hardy volunteers to reinforce the northern outposts.

quest:469.text: Daily Delivery. Daily Delivery is an errand on behalf of the dwarven hunter Einar Stonegrip, who asks travelers heading toward Menethil Harbor to deliver cured crocolisk hides to the local tanner. Rather than facing domestic friction at home, Einar relies on passing adventurers to keep his supply line moving. Out in the marshlands, Einar Stonegrip makes his living hunting the local wildlife, particularly the aggressive crocolisks that lurk along the waterways. While he gathers plenty of valuable skins, delivering them requires a trip home to Menethil Harbor. Reluctant to confront his wife Sida during a rough patch in their marriage, Einar prefers to stay in the field and hand his parcels off to passing travelers instead. The destination for these hides is James Halloran, a tanner operating within Menethil Harbor. Halloran relies on regular deliveries from local hunters to craft boots and cure leather for merchants and sailors passing through the port. Having noticed Einar's week-long absence, the tanner easily deduces the marital spat behind the proxy delivery, musing that his own wife might need to intervene and smooth things over with Sida.

quest:493.text: Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills. Journey to Hillsbrad Foothills is a Horde courier task connecting the Forsaken research efforts in Silverpine Forest with their outpost in Tarren Mill. Entrusted with sensitive notes from Apothecary Renferrel, the traveler journeys south into the disputed Hillsbrad Foothills to deliver vital biological research to Apothecary Lydon. This dispatch reflects the intense pressure Lady Sylvanas Windrunner places upon the Royal Apothecary Society to produce a weapon of mass devastation. Since breaking free from the Lich King's iron grip, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner has harbored a single-minded ambition: the development of a New Plague engineered to eradicate both living enemies and the Scourge. To achieve this, the Royal Apothecary Society operates under relentless pressure from the Banshee Queen. Because distance isolates their laboratories, researchers scattered across Lordaeron must continuously share raw chemical data and test findings to accelerate their sinister breakthrough. Apothecary Renferrel, operating out of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, directs couriers to deliver his recent findings to his colleague, Apothecary Lydon. The trek winds south through the shadowed pine woods and down into the open, rolling pastures of Hillsbrad Foothills. There, nestled beneath the Alterac Mountains, lies Tarren Mill—a vital Forsaken hub and laboratory staging ground.

quest:494.text: Time to Strike. "Time to Strike" is a Horde reconnaissance mission that transitions scouts across the Hillsbrad Foothills border to the military hub of Tarren Mill. Delivering Deathstalker Lesh's coded signal to High Executor Darthalia marks the transition from quiet surveillance to coordinated offensive operations against the local human populace. Perched along the high ground near the border between Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the movements of human settlers and militia in the valley below. The Deathstalkers operate as the eyes and ears of the Undercity, surveying enemy settlements before any military deployment. Rather than risk abandoning her watchpost, Lesh entrusts passing Horde travelers to relay her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

quest:5.text: Jitters' Growling Gut. Stranded and terrified in the ruins of Raven Hill, the paranoid vagrant Jitters is desperate for real sustenance after subsisting on weeds and insects. He begs passing adventurers to travel east to Darkshire and convince Chef Grual to prepare a hot batch of his famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill has become a den of ravenous undead and lurking beasts, leaving the eccentric hermit Jitters trapped in hiding for weeks. Prowling through dilapidated shanties under perpetual gloom, he has survived solely on dirt-dwelling grubs and wild weeds. Starved of civilized comfort, his nerves and stomach are pushed to their absolute limits. Desperate for any reminder of safety, Jitters dreams of the seasoned patties crafted at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He sends travelers across the haunted road to seek out Chef Grual, hoping Grual will agree to whip up a batch of Dusky Crab Cakes to quiet his violently growling gut.

quest:503.text: Gol'dir. Krusk has gone through the documents you procured and concludes that Gol'dir is kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has languished in captivity far too long and needs to be freed. Krusk, in Tarren Mill, has gone through the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to Gol'dir being kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Krusk says the captivity has dragged on far too long and Gol'dir needs to be freed. Gol'dir is held in the top room of the inn at Strahnbrad, and the inn is packed with Syndicate. A Rusted Iron Key opens the lock, and Jailor Borhuin carries it; Borhuin may be in any building of the town.

quest:5042.text: Agamaggan's Strength. Agamaggan's Strength is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By exchanging red Blood Shards harvested across the Barrens, travelers are granted the potent physical might revered by the Razormane tribe's greatest warriors. It fuels Mangletooth's bitter hatred of the rival Bristleback quilboar. The quilboar revere the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan, whose spilled blood is said to have formed the thorny red Blood Shards scattered across the Barrens. To the quilboar, drawing upon these crystals is a sacred rite, imbuing their front-line fighters with terrifying physical might. While held captive in Camp Taurajo, the elder Razormane shaman Mangletooth is eager to impart this strength to Horde champions, claiming your foes will cower just as they do before the Razormane's most formidable champions. Mangletooth's generosity is entirely driven by spite. Captured and caged by the orcs and tauren, the old quilboar harbors a searing grudge against the rival Bristleback tribe, the enemies of his own Razormane. Since he cannot break his chains to slaughter them personally, he uses the ancient gifts of Agamaggan as currency, rewarding anyone who decimates the Bristleback tribes and strips their lands of their sacred Blood Shards.

quest:5043.text: Agamaggan's Agility. Agamaggan's Agility is a repeatable blood shard ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering crystalline blood shards mined from the earth of the Barrens, travelers are blessed with the unerring swiftness and accuracy of the quilboar's ancient boar god. Throughout the Barrens, strange crimson minerals known as blood shards jut from the soil, especially near quilboar encampments and colossal brambles. Quilboar tradition teaches that these crystals were formed from the spilled blood of Agamaggan, the Great Boar Ancient who perished fighting the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. Even locked inside a wooden cage at Camp Taurajo, the elder quilboar Mangletooth retains the knowledge to channel this dormant divine power for anyone willing to supply the stones. Quilboar hunters and scouts pride themselves on ruthless accuracy and blinding quickness in the scrublands. In exchange for four blood shards, Mangletooth invokes the latent energy of the fallen demi-god, infusing the petitioner with the predatory instincts and supple grace of his people's best stalkers. Though he grunts with disdain at outsiders, Mangletooth honors his pact, weaving Agamaggan's power into a temporary mantle of agility.

quest:5044.text: Wisdom of Agamaggan. Wisdom of Agamaggan is a repeatable Horde quest offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By presenting blood shards gathered across the Barrens, spellcasters can partake in the ritualistic magic of the ancient boar god Agamaggan. Held prisoner by the Horde at Camp Taurajo, the quilboar Mangletooth trades the magical secrets of his race for crimson crystals known as blood shards. According to quilboar belief, these shards crystallized from the spilled blood of Agamaggan, the towering boar Demigod who perished in the War of the Ancients. Mangletooth claims the geomancers and shaman of his tribes rely on these shards to channel divine power into their rituals. While other offerings coax physical resilience or swiftness from the shards, the ritual of Wisdom focuses strictly on intellect and arcane capability. For the exchange of four blood shards, Mangletooth invokes the boar god's spirit on behalf of the player, wishing them cunning in their confrontations before parting with an ominous reminder of mortality.

quest:5045.text: Rising Spirit. Rising Spirit is a ritual blessing offered by the captured Razormane geomancer Mangletooth at Camp Taurajo. In exchange for blood shards wrested from his Bristleback rivals, Mangletooth channels the ancient power of Agamaggan to invigorate a champion's willpower and spiritual fortitude. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, the Razormane elder Mangletooth possesses deep knowledge of quilboar geomancy and ancestral magic. While other tribes may boast of raw combat ferocity, Mangletooth takes immense pride in his people's spiritual devotion to their creator, the Great Boar Agamaggan. He teaches that an unbroken spirit is what sustains a warrior when strength alone falters in battle, driving champions onward when defeat seems certain. To invoke this spiritual elevation, Mangletooth demands blood shards—crystallized fragments steeped in the ancient blood of Agamaggan that seeped into the red earth ten thousand years ago. By bringing him shards harvested from across the Barrens, particularly from his Bristleback enemies, you provide the raw spiritual conduit needed for him to weave a blessing of rising spirit that bolsters your will.

quest:5046.text: Razorhide. Razorhide is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering him blood shards infused with the life essence of the Ancient boar god Agamaggan, warriors and wanderers can gain a powerful blessing of hardened skin and resilience before heading into combat. The quilboar trace their ancestry and power directly to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who perished battling the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood soaked into the soils of the Barrens, calcifying into crystalline blood shards that still thrum with ancient power. Even though the quilboar remain sworn enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth—held in a cage at Camp Taurajo—is willing to trade their sacred knowledge in exchange for these precious fragments. Natural quilboar physiology grants them thick hides and protective quills, but tribal warriors invoke Agamaggan's blessing of Razorhide to further shield themselves from enemy blades and claws. By channeling four blood shards, Mangletooth mimics this tribal rite for outsiders, magically bolstering an adventurer's defenses so their bones remain unbroken and their skin resists trauma in the wilds.

quest:5052.text: Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Mangletooth, a captive Razormane quilboar held at Camp Taurajo, reveals the sacred origin of the blood shards scattered throughout the Barrens. Imbued with the fallen demigod Agamaggan's life essence, these red minerals grant potent ancestral magic to anyone skilled enough to channel them. In exchange for the shards, the spiteful prisoner offers to share the primal boons of his god with the Horde. According to quilboar lore, the blood of the Ancient Boar God, Agamaggan, did not merely cause giant thorn mazes to erupt across the arid plains when he fell ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. His divine blood seeped deep beneath the soil, infusing the subterranean minerals and crystallizing into blood-red stones. The quilboar revere these shards as sacred remnants of their creator, harvesting them from both mineral seams and holy grounds to serve as totems of battle and sorcery. Caged at Camp Taurajo by the tauren, Mangletooth harbors a bitter grudge against his own kind, claiming his tribe betrayed and cast him out. Deprived of his freedom and his connection to the magic of his people, he eagerly strikes a bargain with adventurers. By exchanging blood shards, Mangletooth bypasses his captivity to channel Agamaggan's power directly into Horde champions, gleefully unleashing them as an instrument of vengeance against the very quilboar who turned their backs on him. In his captivity, Mangletooth speaks reverently of the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south: Razorfen. To the quilboar tribes, the sprawling briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs are literally formed from the fallen demigod's colossal skeleton and tusks. He warns that Razorfen Downs rests within Agamaggan's gaping maw itself—a holy threshold said to devour and crush any intruders who enter without the Boar God's favor.

quest:506.text: Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir, freed from the Syndicate, has information for Krusk in Tarren Mill. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, visited Gol'dir and spoke of making slaves of the orcs who stand against him, and brought a girl named Elysa who wore the pendant the Warchief desires. A day or two ago, the head of the Syndicate paid Gol'dir a visit. His name was Aliden Perenolde, and he styled himself lord of the land. He confided that he meant to enslave the orcs who resisted him, just as his father and the despised Blackmoore, his mentor, once planned. Gol'dir sends you to bring this to Krusk in Tarren Mill, and will make his own way after settling his business where he is. More important, Perenolde brought his mistress, a slight girl named Elysa. Around her neck hung the pendant the Warchief desires.

quest:516.text: Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a Horde quest directed by Shadow Priest Allister from the Sepulcher. Agents of the Forsaken have caught wind of a hidden conclave of Scourge massing inside a secluded cave tucked into the southern Silverpine hills, aiming to strike them down before an offensive can begin. Word reached Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher that mindless servants of the Lich King were massing deep within southern Silverpine Forest. Left unchecked, these Scourge forces posed an immediate threat to Forsaken operations throughout the region. Rather than waiting for the assault to land, Allister directs scouts to take the initiative and eliminate the gathering horde inside their secluded lair before they can mobilize. Beren's Peril itself is an obscure cavern network carved into the hills south of the Dalaran-aligned settlement of Ambermill. The treacherous terrain makes the cavern easy to overlook, approached only by navigating around the southern slopes. Within its shadows dwell the Ravenclaw drudgers and guardians, entrenched remnants of the plague whose destruction helps ensure the Forsaken maintain their tenuous hold over the forest.

quest:518.text: The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara wants the Crushridge ogres thinned out before any real blow is struck against Mug'Thol, whose ogres now hold the Ruins of Alterac. You are sent to cut down Crushridge maulers. Mug'Thol and the Crushridge ogres have taken the Ruins of Alterac. Melisara says it will be hard to punish Mug'Thol while so many ogres stand around. First their numbers must be reduced, and only after that will the next move be made. Your part is to hunt the Crushridge maulers.

quest:530.text: A Husband's Revenge. A Husband's Revenge is the conclusion to a tragic tale of past betrayal carried into undeath. Raleigh Andrean, a Forsaken residing in the Undercity, charges travelers with tracking down his former friend Valdred Moray, who murdered his wife in life. When Raleigh Andrean received the engraved ring carried from Silverpine Forest, it rekindled memories of his mortal life that undeath had mostly withered away. Among those memories was a profound betrayal: his close friend, Valdred Moray, had murdered Raleigh's wife, Deliah. While the chill of the Scourge and subsequent Forsaken existence dulled Raleigh's capacity for grief and love, his thirst for retribution remained entirely intact.

quest:5321.text: The Sleeper Has Awakened. Kerlonian Evershade, a recently awakened Druid of the Claw, struggles to remain awake on his journey toward Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Entrusted with his Horn of Awakening, travelers must shepherd the lethargic druid along the forested border, rousing him when he drifts into slumber and defending him against wild furbolgs and sinister cultists. For millennia, the Druids of the Claw slept within barrows, communing with the wild spirits across the Emerald Dream. Though the Third War demanded their awakening, shaking off centuries of hibernation does not come easily to every mind. Kerlonian Evershade set out south from Darkshore toward Ashenvale to rendezvous with Liladris Moonriver, but exhaustion overtook him shortly into his trek. Finding himself helplessly prone to sudden naps along the wilds, he relies on a brass Horn of Awakening and passing allies to keep his feet moving. The path connecting Darkshore to Ashenvale is far from tranquil. As Kerlonian meanders southward, his vulnerable state invites aggression from the surrounding wilderness. In Twilight Vale, corrupted Blackwood furbolgs stalk the roadway, while farther south into Ashenvale, members of the shadowy Dark Strand cult lurk in ambush. Escorting the groggy druid requires a vigilant watch, as Kerlonian will simply lie down to sleep wherever he stands unless forcefully roused with the horn.

quest:533.text: Infiltration. In Tarren Mill, Krusk at last hears word and rumor of Gol'dir, an orc held prisoner by the Syndicate. The humans keep moving their captive about, so Krusk has narrowed the search to the Syndicate's large camp, just to the north of town, and wants you to bring back whatever information you can find. Krusk has begun to hear word and rumor of Gol'dir. The Syndicate's humans keep moving the orc about, but the search is narrowing to their large camp, just to the north of Tarren Mill. Krusk sends you there to lay hands on whatever information you can and carry it back. Krusk fears that with each day Gol'dir's prospects darken.

quest:5361.text: Family Tree. Cliffwatcher Longhorn asks you to carry a report to Nataka Longhorn, Cliffwatcher's brother, who is stationed in Desolace. Word of unusual centaur activity is meant to reach Ghost Walker Post. Nataka, Cliffwatcher's brother, holds a posting at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. A year has passed since Cliffwatcher last wrote, and in that time the centaurs have been behaving unusually. Nataka should hear of it, and you are asked to carry the report. The way runs to Stonetalon Mountain, which lies north of the Crossroads, then west into the Charred Vale. From there it turns south into Desolace, where a road runs south to Ghost Walker Post.

quest:5381.text: Hand of Iruxos. Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village says the Burning Blade holds a Demon Box, and that something powerful called the Hand of Iruxos is kept inside. At Mannoroc Coven, the Burning Blade makes use of it to open demon portals. Taiga sends you to Thunder Axe Fortress to fetch the box. Taiga Wisemane wants the flow of demons into our world stopped. You are given a demon pick, to be used on the red crystal inside Thunder Axe Fortress, which opens the way to the Demon Box. The box and the pick are to be brought back to Taiga in Shadowprey Village.

quest:5386.text: Catch of the Day. Cooked fish has not been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long time, and Nataka Longhorn would like that to change. Nataka rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers around, yet all the centaur activity leaves little time for the journey. You are asked to go in Nataka's place and bring back two Bloodbelly fish. No cooked fish has been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long while. Nataka Longhorn rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers, but with so much centaur activity there is little time to make the journey. So you are asked to go there, talk with the local fisherman Jinar'Zillen, and return with two Bloodbelly fish, Nataka's favorite. The road south of the post bends west and brings you to the troll village.

quest:540.text: Preserving Knowledge. Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore sends you into the Ruins of Alterac, where ogres have settled among the precious books left behind. Tomes the ogres looted must be recovered, and one above all: a worn leather book holding The Arm of Gri'lek, a work of ancient troll lore. Ogres have made their home in the ruins of Alterac, and Dibbs dreads what they might be doing to the books still there. You are to go in, hunt for the tomes the ogres have looted, and recover whatever you can. Dibbs would search the ruins too, but fears old bones would not survive the climb into the mountains. Among all the tomes, Dibbs most wants one book: the worn leather volume containing The Arm of Gri'lek. Dibbs is bent on learning the ancient troll lore inside, and the Ruins of Alterac were the last known home of an intact copy.

quest:5421.text: Fish in a Bucket. Jinar'Zillen of Shadowprey Village in Desolace likes to do as little as possible. Many shellfish traps sit below the village docks, and anyone who gathers the shellfish from them will be repaid with something worth having. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village, and would far rather someone else did the collecting. Anyone willing to take on that work is promised something they want in return: one fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

quest:544.text: Prison Break In. Magus Wordeen Voidglare is in Tarren Mill on research but now faces a crisis. A few months ago four Forsaken fled the Undercity after stealing artifacts from a secure vault, and Sylvanas wants them back. Voidglare came to Tarren Mill to research and now must resolve a crisis. Four Forsaken turned their backs on their brethren and, worse, stole from the Dark Lady. They broke into a secure vault and took four artifacts the apothecaries required for certain studies. Sylvanas wants them returned. The thieves ran from the Undercity to Dalaran, where the wizards put them in quarantine at the Lordamere Internment Camp. You are to find the traitors, take back the artifacts and report to Voidglare in Tarren Mill. There are four: a Bloodstone Wedge, Marble, Shard and Oval. Dermot has the wedge, Ricter the marble, Alina the shard and Kegan Darkmar the oval.

quest:545.text: Dalaran Patrols. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill cares nothing for why the wizards of Dalaran raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. What matters is that the ruined outskirts beyond the dome may conceal treasures of real magical worth, while the wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. Voidglare wants those patrols thinned. After Prison Break In, Voidglare turns to the wizards of Dalaran, who raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. Some say it shelters them from the violence of the age; others say they simply wanted solitude to study and plot. Voidglare does not care which. The ruined outskirts beyond the dome may conceal treasures of real magical worth, but the wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. You are to hunt six Dalaran Summoners and twelve Elemental Slaves, then return to Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

quest:5501.text: Bone Collector. At Kormek's Hut in Desolace, the goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle is certain that kodo bones are about to transform the world. Ten of them are wanted from the Kodo Graveyard, south of the hut, and something is promised in return. Bibbly insists the hut is sitting on a goldmine. Customers make furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder from kodo bones. Bibbly sends you south to the Kodo Graveyard to bring back ten of them, with something promised in return. A caravan comes by to pick up Bibbly's kodo bones, then sells them at Shadowprey Village. It is due any moment, and Bibbly is ten bones short of what is called a career high.

quest:552.text: Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand in Tarren Mill means to avenge Master Helcular, a great wizard on the brink of becoming a lich, who was killed by a human lynch mob after it found his ritual lair. Before vengeance can fall on Southshore, Thaivand needs Helcular's Rod, which one of the yeti there must hold. Master Helcular was on the brink of becoming a lich when he was found and killed by a human lynch mob, who had discovered the ritual lair he kept in the hills. They then buried the body in the Southshore cemetery. His apprentice, Thaivand, finds this disregard for a great wizard unacceptable and vows that the rains of vengeance will fall upon the town of Southshore. Thaivand says Helcular's Rod is needed first. Yeti have overtaken the ritual lair, and Thaivand is sure one of the beasts has the rod. There are so many yeti in the region that finding it will be difficult. Growless Cave and Darrow Hill are among the places they can be found.

quest:553.text: Helcular's Revenge. Novice Thaivand hands you the Rod of Helcular. Three ceremonial pyres that Helcular fashioned for his most powerful spell must each charge it, and then it is to be driven into Helcular's grave in Southshore. Helcular fashioned three ceremonial pyres for his most powerful spell, and the rod must be charged from each one. The flames of Azel and Veraz lie within the Foothill Caverns, in the yeti cave at Darrow Hill. The third, the Flame of Uzel, is found in a small cave above the caverns, farther north in the mountains, near Growless Cave. Once the rod is charged from all three flames, it is to be driven into Helcular's grave at Southshore, a heavily guarded human town. The graveyard sits in the northeast corner of the town, by the river, and the grave lies at the graveyard's southeastern corner.

quest:5561.text: Kodo Roundup. At Scrabblescrew's Camp in Desolace, Smeed Scrabblescrew is expecting a caravan and wants five tamed kodos ready for it. You carry Smeed's kodo kombobulator out among the ancient, aged and dying kodos, and lead the ones it tames back to the camp. Bibbly believes no other goblin in Desolace knows how to turn a profit. Smeed Scrabblescrew disagrees: the one caravan willing to brave this land depends on Smeed, and Smeed has formed a partnership with Cork and Rigger. The caravan is due at the camp shortly. Smeed built a device that can rejuvenate and bring under control aged and dying kodos. Aimed at an ancient, aged or dying kodo, it jolts the beast into a tamed kodo that follows you. You bring five of them back to Scrabblescrew's Camp, along with the device.

quest:557.text: Bracers of Binding. Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill says the Magus, busy with the stone tokens you gathered, will eventually want their counterpart: bracers of binding. You are to collect four Bracers of Earth Binding from elementals among the ruins of Dalaran. While the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Bel'varil expects a further wish: samples of the matching piece, bracers of binding. Worn on an elemental's wrists, they tie it to a mage's service. Among the ruins of Dalaran, elementals wear them. Bel'varil wants four Bracers of Earth Binding brought to Tarren Mill.

quest:5581.text: Portals of the Legion. After Hand of Iruxos, Taiga Wisemane in Shadowprey Village shows you the Hand and asks you to banish six demon portals at Mannoroc Coven, warning you to be wary of the portal guardians. Taiga Wisemane holds up the Hand of Iruxos, a grisly thing to look at, and says you must carry it if the demon portals around Mannoroc Coven are ever to be closed. The demon threat is increasing, and shutting the portals will check the number of demons crossing into this world. She wants all six portals banished, and she warns you to be wary of their guardians.

quest:564.text: Costly Menace. Darren Malvew of Southshore hates losing the town's beautiful horses. Undead, the Syndicate gang and assorted scoundrels have cost plenty, but Darren says nothing threatens them more than the mountain lions that keep coming down from the hills of Alterac. Darren Malvew of Southshore cannot stand losing the beautiful horses there. Quite a few have been lost to undead creeps, the Syndicate gang and the scoundrels poking about the region. By Darren's own word, though, no menace to the horses is bigger than the mountain lions up in Alterac, forever coming down from the hills. Darren wants the lions dealt with: eight Mountain Lions and ten Hulking Mountain Lions. Mountain Lions are found in the lower hills of the Alterac Mountains.

quest:5643.text: Shadowguard. Shadowguard is a priestly calling issued to Darkspear troll priests who find themselves far from home in the Forsaken capital of Undercity. Aelthalyste recognizes that the young troll has matured enough for their tribe's sacred rites and sends them back to Orgrimmar. In the Valley of Spirits, the priest trainer Ur'kyo awaits to guide them into a vital tier of spiritual protection. Even in the gloom of the Undercity, the bonds of faith and tribal tradition remain strong. Forsaken priest trainer Aelthalyste observes visiting troll priests closely, noting when an initiate has grown potent enough to face their culture's trials. Rather than imposing the bleak philosophy of the Forsaken priesthood upon them, she directs the troll back across the Great Sea to the ancestral ways of their own elders. Upon arriving in Durotar, the priest makes their way to the mystic enclave of the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. There, Ur'kyo tends to the spiritual needs and ancient rituals of the Darkspear tribe. He welcomes the returning initiate, preparing them for an essential rite of passage that bridges the priest's bond to the loa with practical spells vital for warding off harm.

quest:5644.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of passage quest for Forsaken priests journeying far from Lordaeron. Guided by the Forsaken priest trainer Miles Welsh in Thunder Bluff, the adept is directed back across the seas to Aelthalyste in the Undercity to unlock a signature manifestation of Shadow magic. While visiting Thunder Bluff, Forsaken priests who have honed their mastery over divine and shadowy disciplines are evaluated by Miles Welsh, a Forsaken priest posted among the tauren. Recognizing that an acolyte has grown sufficiently in power, Miles bids them return to the Ruins of Lordaeron rather than attempt to impart these higher mysteries himself in Kalimdor. Awaiting beneath the city ruins within the Undercity's War Quarter is Aelthalyste, one of the foremost mentors of Forsaken priesthood. She watches over the development of shadow-weaving acolytes, ensuring that the potent, draining blight known as the Devouring Plague is entrusted only to those capable of wielding its corruptive force without succumbing to it.

quest:5645.text: A Lack of Fear. A Lack of Fear is a rite-of-passage summons for dwarven priests, calling promising disciples back to the grand halls of Ironforge. High Priest Rohan awaits in the Mystic Ward to test their discipline and bestow teachings tailored to their growing resilience. Priests serving the Alliance abroad are routinely directed by their local mentors to report back to their order's senior clergy. For dwarven disciples, that guidance leads straight to High Priest Rohan in the heart of Ironforge's Mystic Ward. The summons marks a turning point where basic spiritual practice gives way to deeper, trial-tested applications of holy magic. High Priest Rohan does not simply teach liturgy; dwarven tradition views the Light as a shield and an unyielding bulwark in physical conflict. Reporting for this test acknowledges that the initiate has survived baptism through fire in the wider world and possesses the mettle required to master fear itself on the front lines.

quest:5646.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite-of-passage quest for Forsaken priests who have ventured to Kalimdor to learn from the Darkspear tribe. The troll priest trainer Ur'kyo in Orgrimmar directs promising Forsaken initiates to return home to Undercity, where Aelthalyste waits to impart deeper teachings of shadow. While the orcs and tauren have little inclination toward priestly worship, the Darkspear trolls and the Forsaken share a curious theological bond within the Horde. In Orgrimmar, the troll priest trainer Ur'kyo guides those drawn to spiritual power. Yet he recognizes that Forsaken initiates must ultimately master the sinister arts unique to their own condition. In a mutual show of respect between their peoples, Ur'kyo directs wandering Forsaken back to Lordaeron to complete their training. Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, Priestess Aelthalyste tends to the flock in the Undercity's War Quarter. Forsaken priests walk a solitary, grueling path shaped by their turn toward shadow, tempering the painful touch of the Holy Light with the devastating affliction of Shadow magic. When an initiate attains sufficient prowess, Aelthalyste gathers them close to bestow the affliction known to their kind as the Devouring Plague.

quest:5672.text: Elune's Grace. Elune's Grace is a rite of recognition offered to devout night elf priests in Darnassus. Upon proving their faith and discipline through their early journeys, priests are called before Priestess Alathea to receive deeper instruction in the divine mysteries of the Moon Goddess. Within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, the Sisterhood of Elune guides young acolytes from their first prayers to mastery of lunar magic. Night elves do not look upon the Holy Light in the same manner as humans or dwarves; their faith is inextricably tied to the Mother Moon, Elune. When a novice priest reaches a significant milestone in their devotion, senior mentors take notice, marking the disciple as ready to shoulder greater divine power. Priestess Alathea extends this summons on behalf of the Sisterhood. She acknowledges that the acolyte's dedication has elevated them beyond the common flock, granting them access to traditions preserved across millennia. Accepting the rite seals the priest's bond to Elune, unlocking specific protective wards and lunar invocations unique to the kaldorei faith.

quest:5674.text: Elune's Grace. Elune's Grace is a rite of advancement for developing night elf priests, marking their readiness to wield divine talents unique to their people. Guided from local outposts like Dolanaar back to the sacred Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, candidates present themselves before Priestess Alathea to prove their devotion. Within the Sisterhood of Elune, a priest's journey involves more than simply mastering standard prayers of mending and smiting.
