As acolytes grow in experience, they reach a threshold where they are deemed ready to receive blessings granted exclusively to the kaldorei. Local mentors such as Laurna Morninglight in Dolanaar lack the authority to bestow these deeper arts, directing promising disciples back to the cultural and spiritual heart of their order. The quest directs initiates across Teldrassil to the grand Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. There, beneath the gaze of the high priesthood, Priestess Alathea evaluates whether the petitioner is truly prepared to bear the goddess's defensive mantle. Learning Elune's Grace symbolizes reaching true maturity within the priesthood, bridging the gap between raw potential and formal service to the goddess.

quest:5676.text: Arcane Feedback. Arcane Feedback is a rite of passage for Alliance priests in Stormwind City, granted by High Priestess Laurena in the Cathedral of Light. Reaching a deeper communion with faith, the priest is instructed in wards designed to counter hostile practitioners of the arcane. It represents the Church's practical defense against raw sorcery and rogue spellcasters. Within the sunlit cloisters of the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena reminds acolytes of an enduring peril: arcane magic. While the Holy Light brings healing, warmth, and divine order, raw magical energies are volatile and often court corruption or catastrophe. To endure against warlocks, renegade sorcerers, and magical beasts, devout priests are taught that faith alone must sometimes be shaped into an active ward against ambient spells. Arcane Feedback trains the mind and spirit to punish hostile spellcasters for channeling power against the faithful. Rather than simply deflecting magical volleys, this discipline mirrors arcane energy back into its source, burning through the caster's own mana reserves while causing agony. Laurena imparts this spell to human priests stepping out into the wider world, ensuring the Cathedral's emissaries never travel defenseless against sorcery.

quest:5677.text: Arcane Feedback. Arcane Feedback is a priest quest given by High Priest Rohan in Ironforge to human acolytes visiting Khaz Modan. Rohan directs the developing priest home to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind to receive teachings tailored specifically to the traditions of humankind. It marks a key moment of progression where young disciples begin mastering racial manifestations of their faith. When a human priest seeks advanced spiritual tutelage in the halls of the Mystic Ward, High Priest Rohan greets them with reverence but sets a boundary. While dwarven and human priests share devotion to the Holy Light, each civilization nurtures its own particular rites, disciplines, and defensive prayers. Rather than imparting Ironforge's unique secrets, Rohan sends human clergy back to their cultural roots in Elwynn, ensuring they master their people's distinct heritage. Upon returning to Stormwind City, the acolyte reports to High Priestess Laurena within the grand Cathedral of Light. Laurena is relieved to see Rohan's guidance reach the traveler, welcoming them back just as their nascent powers begin to flourish. This return paves the way for deeper initiation into the Kingdom of Stormwind's spiritual practices, preparing practitioners to wield the Holy Light against the rising threats encircling the realm.

quest:5678.text: Arcane Feedback. "Arcane Feedback" is an Alliance priest quest that directs human priests training in Darnassus back home to Stormwind. Sent by Priestess Alathea at the Temple of the Moon, the journey highlights the deep cultural rift regarding magic between the night elves and the Eastern Kingdoms. Upon returning to the Cathedral of Light, High Priestess Laurena prepares the acolyte for deeper theological instruction. Priestess Alathea oversees visiting priests within the tranquil halls of the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. While she recognizes the formal alliance between the kaldorei and the humans of Stormwind, she harbors deep misgivings about human magical and spiritual practices. Night elf society views arcane power as inherently volatile and dangerous, shaped by ten millennia of grief following the War of the Ancients. Even divine rites from humanity that blur the lines between radiant faith and arcane mechanics make night elf clergy distinctly uneasy. Despite her hesitation, Alathea honors the bond between the Alliance races and releases the visiting acolyte to answer a recall from the Cathedral of Light. High Priestess Laurena has sent couriers across the seas to gather growing human priests for advanced training. Stepping back into Stormwind, the acolyte leaves behind the moonlit groves of Elune to embrace the grand stone sanctuaries and golden radiance of the Holy Light.

quest:5679.text: Devouring Plague. Devouring Plague is a rite of instruction offered to Forsaken priests who have proven their dedication to shadow magic. Granted by Priestess Aelthalyste in the Undercity, the teaching marks an acolyte's initiation into one of the most dreaded curses woven by the undead priesthood. In the murky cloisters of the War Quarter, Priestess Aelthalyste guides Forsaken practitioners through the grim arts of the Shadow. While living priests of other races appeal to the Holy Light or ancestral spirits for their power, the Forsaken have forged their own spiritual doctrines. Devouring Plague represents the crystallization of their philosophy: inflicting suffering upon their foes while leeching the stolen vitality back into their own decaying bodies. Aelthalyste does not offer the knowledge of the plague lightly. The spell is considered a weapon of potent malice, intended to turn the tide against the Scourge and the Scarlet Crusade. When imparting the spell, Aelthalyste warns her disciples to hone their command over it through relentless practice, cautioning that far greater trials lie ahead for those who seek to master the dark arts.

quest:568.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard the Horde's foothold in Stranglethorn Vale and protect their supply chain to Stonard. To keep that supply chain safe, he directs Horde champions to thin out the Lashtail Raptors outside Grom'gol Base Camp. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Commander Aggro'gosh carries the duty of protecting every member of the Horde within the jungle. The camp exists to keep supplies flowing safely to Stonard, but some of the local inhabitants are standing in the way. The raptors outside Grom'gol are the ones in the way. Aggro'gosh calls upon loyal fighters to thin out the Lashtail Raptors there, then report back to him for reassignment.

quest:569.text: The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard Grom'gol's supply lines through Stranglethorn Vale. After the earlier hunt thinning the raptors outside the camp, a band of ogres encamped at the nearby Mizjah Ruins continues to harass supply caravans heading toward Stonard. The Horde's presence in northern Stranglethorn Vale is centered on supplying Stonard, an outpost of vital strategic interest. While Commander Aggro'gosh did not arrive with the intention of fighting every native group, a band of local Mosh'Ogg ogres has claimed the Mizjah Ruins southeast of the camp. Warnings have failed to stop their continuous raids against Horde supply shipments, prompting the commander to order a strike against the ogre brutes and witch doctors holding the ruins.

quest:570.text: Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin seeks to harness the natural magic of Stranglethorn Vale for the benefit of the Horde. Building upon his previous rituals at Grom'gol Base Camp, he asks for sharp claws and a pristine feline fang to weave a powerful enchantment. Within Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin works to understand and bend the feral power of the wild to strengthen the Horde. Having seen success in his initial rites, he promises to craft a specialized enchanted relic for those willing to brave the dense underbrush and stalk the deadly predators prowling the surrounding territory. The ritual demands eight claws taken from shadowmaw panthers and a pristine fang from a tigress. Mok'thardin notes that while these fierce felines wander across Stranglethorn Vale, a gathering of them prowls south-eastward, just past the river running by the Mizjah Ruins.

quest:574.text: Special Forces. Following the reduction of the rogue colonel's rank-and-file soldiers, Sergeant Yohwa asks you to target the elite core of the compound. You are sent into the Stockpile cave to eliminate the commandos and headshrinkers before reporting to Lieutenant Doren. With the regular soldiers of the Kurzen Compound diminished through the work of the Second Rebellion, Sergeant Yohwa sets her sights on the colonel's elite specialists. She knows many of Kurzen's troops personally and calls them skilled, loyal and cruel. When they are not out in the wilderness slaughtering rebel soldiers, they are found in a cave at the back of the compound called the Stockpile. To break their strength, you are sent into the cavern to dispatch ten Kurzen Commandos and six Kurzen Headshrinkers. After the fight, Sergeant Yohwa tells you to report to her commanding officer, Lieutenant Doren, at the Rebel Camp, who will want your account firsthand.

quest:5741.text: Sceptre of Light. Azore Aldamort has heard that the Burning Blade of Thunder Axe Fortress, to the east, now hold the Sceptre of Light, which word says they obtained from the naga. Legend says it could sink whole cities beneath the great seas, and Azore will not let the Burning Blade keep such power. You are asked to bring it back to Ethel Rethor. Word has it that the naga's Sceptre of Light has come into the hands of the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress. Legend says it can sink whole cities beneath the great seas. Azore Aldamort holds that the Burning Blade cannot be allowed such power. A Burning Blade seer keeps the sceptre and studies it from the top of one of the fortress watchtowers. Azore wants you to take it from there yourself and carry it back to the tower at Ethel Rethor.

quest:5763.text: Hunting in Stranglethorn. Roon Wildmane, a tauren in Desolace, once hunted beside a dwarf named Hemet. Now Roon sends you off with a kodo horn, bound for Hemet Nesingwary in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long ago a dwarf named Hemet came to Desolace, eager to hunt great beasts. Hemet handled a rifle with uncanny skill, and the two hunters passed many days together, the old enmity between their peoples set aside. When Hemet went off to Stranglethorn, Roon vowed to welcome Hemet back one day for another hunt, and Roon decides that time has arrived. You are to carry Roon's kodo horn to Hemet, who will know whose it is. Look in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp.

quest:578.text: The Stone of the Tides. Following rumours of a haunted isle off the jungle coast, Baron Revilgaz suspects an ancient troll relic has resurfaced. He directs explorers to scout the mysterious landmass and delivers a pass to research the artifact within the archives of Stormwind. Having learned of strange apparitions and water elementals haunting an offshore island in Stranglethorn Vale, Baron Revilgaz sees an opportunity. Suspecting that the goblin mage Gazban may have uncovered the fabled Stone of the Tides, the ruler of Booty Bay sends you to locate the island and confirm whether the rumors are true. To satisfy any curiosity about the relic, he provides a library scrip redeemable among the scholars in Stormwind.

quest:581.text: Hunt for Yenniku. Nimboya has returned from Orgrimmar to the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale to search for Yenniku, the youngest son of his chieftain. Suspecting the Bloodscalp tribe holds the youth captive, the scout asks you to hunt their warriors and take their tusks to demonstrate your strength. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nimboya speaks of a grim fate looming over Yenniku, the youngest son of the Darkspear chieftain. In accordance with an old tribal custom, the boy had been placed among the Gurubashi trolls of Zul'Gurub. When the Darkspear tribe departed their homeland alongside the orc warchief Thrall, Yenniku was left behind and lost. Sent back from distant Orgrimmar, Nimboya has undertaken the responsibility of finding the chieftain's son and bringing him to safety. Nimboya believes the Bloodscalp tribe now holds Yenniku. He demands proof that an adventurer is strong enough to hunt them. You are directed north to hunt Bloodscalp trolls and gather nine of their tusks. Bringing these trophies back to Grom'gol Base Camp proves your martial prowess and begins a longer pursuit to locate the chieftain's boy, leading directly into the hunt known as Headhunting.

quest:582.text: Headhunting. Nimboya at Grom'gol Base Camp needs to determine whether Yenniku, the son of the Darkspear chieftain, is dead. Adventurers are asked to hunt Bloodscalp headhunters and recover their shrunken heads so Nimboya can examine them. Following the search begun in Hunt for Yenniku, Nimboya worries that the chieftain's son may have already perished at the hands of the Bloodscalp tribe. To find out, he asks you to hunt the Bloodscalp Headhunters roaming the ruins of Zuuldaia and Zul'Kunda up the northern coast. By gathering twenty shrunken heads from them, Nimboya hopes to inspect the grisly trophies and confirm whether Yenniku met a violent end, cursing the Bloodscalp chief Gan'zulah if the youth was indeed slain.

quest:5821.text: Bodyguard for Hire. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally lead their kodo past the Kolkar centaur village, yet they stop whenever the centaur war drums are heard. Cork asks you to protect the caravan past the Kolkar village, and payment is waiting with Smeed Scrabblescrew, a bit down the road. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally take their kodo straight past the Kolkar centaur. Now and then the centaur war drums are heard, and the caravan stops, because dead traders make no profit. Cork asks you to guard the caravan past the Kolkar village, a short distance, and keep it in one piece. The caravan waits north of the Kolkar Village and southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress. Payment waits with Smeed Scrabblescrew at Scrabblescrew's Camp, a bit down the road. Smeed does a little business with the Gizelton caravan.

quest:583.text: Welcome to the Jungle. Barnil Stonepot welcomes newcomers arriving at the hunting camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Recognizing a fellow battle-tested wanderer, he arranges an introduction to the expedition's leader, the renowned huntsman Hemet Nesingwary. Barnil Stonepot greets newcomers at the camp in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, and he can tell a seasoned combatant when he sees one. He points out Hemet Nesingwary, a famous Alliance war hero and peerless tracker. Nesingwary reserves his fellowship for proven veterans, and Barnil believes the old marksman might be convinced to share his hunting wisdom with someone who has endured the trials of battle.

quest:5943.text: Gizelton Caravan. Rigger Gizelton and Cork launched their caravan to get rich, and found the trade more dangerous than they expected. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead, and Rigger wants a capable adventurer to guard the caravan past it. Rigger Gizelton and Cork set up the caravan to make a fortune, and had no idea how risky turning a profit could be. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead. The demons usually leave the caravan alone, but this time the kodos are spooked. Rigger offers payment if you protect the caravan past the coven. Once it is safely through, your pay waits with Smeed, a business associate of theirs, at Scrabblescrew's Camp.

quest:596.text: Bloody Bone Necklaces. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp has his own agenda in Stranglethorn Vale beyond assisting Nimboya. He seeks to weaken the rival Bloodscalp tribe by gathering trophies from their warriors. Though Kin'weelay arrived in the jungle outpost of Grom'gol Base Camp to help Nimboya, he maintains private purposes of his own. The Bloodscalp trolls dwelling to the north are enemies of the Darkspears. Kin'weelay believes that claiming personal trophies from fallen foes bestows spiritual power over them, asking travelers to hunt Bloodscalp warriors and take the bloody bone necklaces they wear around their necks.

quest:601.text: Water Elementals. Following discoveries regarding the Stone of the Tides, Baron Revilgaz seeks a way to counteract the artifact's curse. He sends adventurers back to the island to harvest bracers from conjured water elementals so their magical residue can be inspected by experts. Believing the water elementals were summoned by the goblin wizard Gazban, Baron Revilgaz suspects their magical residue holds clues to dealing with the Stone of the Tides. The stone is said to curse anyone who wields it, causing the bearer to drift in and out of reality. To find a countermeasure, Revilgaz directs you back to the island off the coast to gather elemental bracers that might be scrutinized by the scholarly mages of Dalaran. Upon receiving the bracers, Revilgaz admits he lacks the specialized expertise to tell whether any of them will be of use. Rather than travel to Dalaran himself—he will not leave Booty Bay just to chat with tiresome old mages—he sends you north to have a mage look at them.

quest:602.text: Magical Analysis. Baron Revilgaz directs you northward from Booty Bay to consult the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Taking a bag of water elemental bracers, you seek out Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver to decipher the arcane curse tied to the Stone of the Tides. Following your hunt for the water elemental bracers, Baron Revilgaz hands over a bundle of their bracers. The goblin leader knows that unraveling the curse behind the Stone of the Tides requires deeper magical expertise than Booty Bay can provide. He directs you north toward the ruins of Dalaran, where the wizards remain deeply engaged in rebuilding their broken kingdom. Convinced that arcane scholars cannot ignore an intriguing puzzle, Revilgaz recommends seeking Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver directly, having had dealings with the knowledgeable wizard in the past.

quest:6027.text: Book of the Ancients. Azore Aldamort of the Ethel Rethor tower trusts you with a gem. Set in the hand of a serpent statue on Ranazjar Isle, northwest of the tower, it calls up the protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. After Sceptre of Light, Azore Aldamort hands you the Gem of the Serpent. A Serpent Statue stands on Ranazjar Isle, a little island to the northwest of the Ethel Rethor tower, and the gem belongs on its hand. That will bring forth the guardian of the Book of the Ancients, a book that holds naga secrets kept for centuries. Azore hopes it will teach much about their scaled foes.

quest:603.text: Ansirem's Key. Following his magical examination, Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver points toward an ancient troll dagger capable of disrupting the focal altar empowering the Stone of the Tides. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay. Ansirem Runeweaver determines that an altar or focal point amplifies the power of the Stone of the Tides. Overpowering that magic calls for another troll relic: an ancient dagger he found while researching in Stranglethorn. He passed it long ago to his daughter Catelyn, a headstrong girl who left home for the pirates of Booty Bay.

quest:605.text: Singing Blue Shards. Crank Fizzlebub seeks an enterprising adventurer to gather Singing Crystal Shards from the basilisks of Stranglethorn Vale. Competition with the Venture Company prevents him from harvesting the mineral deposits directly, leaving basilisk hides as the next best option. He promises a cut of the profits to anyone willing to bring him ten decent specimens. Crank Fizzlebub has identified an eager market for the Singing Crystals unique to Stranglethorn Vale. Unfortunately for his business ambitions, the aggressive presence of the Venture Company makes it hard for him to gather raw crystal in the field. To circumvent his rivals, Fizzlebub turns to an alternative method: basilisks consume the crystals, incorporating the mineral into their hardened hides, which allows usable shards to be retrieved from them instead. While any basilisk in the jungle might yield acceptable crystal fragments, Fizzlebub says the gentler ones are found along the shores south of Zul'Kunda, up north. Gathering ten shards allows him to move forward with his buyers, after which his business concerns shift toward the operations of the Venture Company itself.

quest:610.text: "Pretty Boy" Duncan. After tracking down Catelyn the Blade on behalf of her father, an adventurer learns that her weapon is no longer in her hands. She demands that her lost dagger be retrieved from a pirate named Pretty Boy Duncan before she cooperates further. Following the trail from Ansirem's Key leads directly to Catelyn the Blade, who ran away from a quiet life of scholarship and dusty tomes alongside mages. She cannot hand over her dagger at her father's request, since she no longer has it. If anyone hopes to secure her blade, they will first have to deal with the Bloodsail Buccaneer who took it. Catelyn suffered an uncharacteristic defeat at the hands of Pretty Boy Duncan, who struck her unconscious and made off with her signature weapon. As a fighter who relies on her personal knife, she insists on recovering that exact weapon from the buccaneer before anything else can move forward.

quest:6132.text: Get Me Out of Here!. Melizza Brimbuzzle traveled into the Valley of Spears hoping to do business with the Maraudines, but they would not talk, and she fears they mean to eat her. She asks you to get her out of there; her brother Hornizz will pay you handsomely. Melizza walked into the Valley of Spears to speak with the Maraudines, thinking she could strike a deal. They would not talk, and she suspects they would rather eat her. She says she overheard centaurs only minutes ago discussing wood for their cookpot, and she wants out quickly. Hornizz Brimbuzzle waits at the family camp, east of here and beside the kodo graveyard. Melizza promises that her brother will pay you well for bringing her out of the valley.

quest:6134.text: Ghost-o-plasm Round Up. Hornizz Brimbuzzle thinks there is money in the ghosts of the Valley of Bones. He figures the Magram centaurs would pay plenty for ghost energy, and he gives you a crate of ghost magnets to draw the spirits out. Hornizz points you southeast, to the Valley of Bones, where Magram ghosts walk. It sounds frightening, he admits, but surely it is scarier still for the Magram. He is sure that ghost energy captured there would be worth plenty to those centaurs. He hands you a crate of ghost magnets. Set down between the two huge skeletons in the valley, known as the Dead Goliaths, a magnet lures the ghosts toward it. From them you take ghost-o-plasm, which is what Hornizz plans to sell to the Magram. He wants eight ghost-o-plasms brought back to him, along with the crate.

quest:6141.text: Brother Anton. Brother Crowley speaks of Brother Anton, a fellow warrior who learned of undead in distant Kalimdor and booked passage at once to destroy them. Anton is looking for people with bravery and resolve, and waits in Nijel's Point in Desolace. Brother Crowley says rumors of an undead infestation in Desolace, a land in far-off Kalimdor, reached Anton, who immediately booked passage to seek and destroy the menace. Anton wants help from those with bravery and resolve. If your heart is true, Crowley tells you to speak with Anton in Nijel's Point, the Alliance town in Desolace.

quest:6142.text: Clam Bait. Mai'Lahii at Shadowprey Village has fished all his life and says the best bait is soft-shelled clam meat, which no fish can resist. He wants ten pieces, to be found around a wrecked ship up the coast to the north. Mai'Lahii has fished all his life, and he swears by soft-shelled clam meat as bait, since the fish cannot resist it. To the north, off the coast, lies a wrecked ship, and soft-shelled clams are scattered throughout that area. He asks for ten pieces of the meat.

quest:6143.text: Other Fish to Fry. Drulzegar Skraghook, a fisherman at Shadowprey Village in Desolace, lost the entire crew to the naga while fishing near Ranazjar Isle. Guilt weighs on Drulzegar, who asks you to go after the Slitherblade. Drulzegar Skraghook and the crew fished by Ranazjar Isle, which lies north of a wreck on the coast, and had done so many times. One morning the naga attacked and killed everyone except Drulzegar. Since then revenge is all Drulzegar thinks about, and the guilt is too much to bear. Drulzegar wants seven Slitherblade Myrmidons, seven Slitherblade Naga and five Slitherblade Sorceresses slain. A bad knee keeps Drulzegar from going along. The naga, Drulzegar says, usually lurk far down among the coral reefs beneath the waves, and the effort will be rewarded.

quest:616.text: The Haunted Isle. Krazek keeps his ears open for unusual rumors throughout Booty Bay on behalf of Baron Revilgaz. A tale shared by tavern sailors speaks of a haunted island off the coast, inhabited by water elementals and the ghost of a raving goblin. Delivering this rumor to Revilgaz piques the baron's interest in an ancient troll legend. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Krazek gathers word of anything unusual happening throughout Stranglethorn Vale at the request of Baron Revilgaz. While Krazek normally pays little heed to spectral gossip, stories told by sailors drinking in the local tavern caught his attention. They speak of an offshore isle occupied by water elementals and haunted by a raving goblin ghost, so he asks you to relay the story to the baron. Upon hearing Krazek's report of the haunted isle, Baron Revilgaz recalls an old troll legend he once read about in a book. The presence of water elementals and the goblin apparition leads the baron to suspect that an ancient relic, the Stone of the Tides, might finally be within his grasp to add to his personal collection of artifacts.

quest:6161.text: Claim Rackmore's Treasure!. Rackmore's log tells of a ship bound for Feathermoon Stronghold that was set upon by creatures of the sea. To keep his treasure from his enemies, Rackmore hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle, and the silver key and golden key that open it are lost. The log says Rackmore's ship was on its way to Feathermoon Stronghold when seafaring creatures attacked it. Hoping to keep his treasure from his enemies, he hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle. Two keys open it, one silver and one gold, and both were lost. Someone who finds the keys and the chest will find a treasure.

quest:627.text: Favor for Krazek. While repairing a crock pot brought down to Booty Bay, the goblin Krazek demands a personal favor in return. He wants rare lesser bloodstone ore retrieved from a distant cave in the northern hills before he will hand back the repaired cookware. After accepting the broken cookware in Booty Bay, Krazek pauses his tinkering to ask for a trade. Rather than repairing the pot for free, he directs you far northward into the Arathi Highlands. Within a cave in Drywhisker Gorge lies lesser bloodstone ore, a low-grade yet prized mineral sought after by those who understand its properties. Krazek promises to work on fixing the pot while you make the long journey north. He expects four loads of the bloodstone brought back to the port, offering payment in exchange for the favor if you return with enough samples. He also makes it clear that if you lack the knowledge to extract the ore yourself, you will need to rely on someone who does.

quest:6284.text: Arachnophobia. Arachnophobia is a Horde bounty quest targeting Besseleth, an ancient and colossal predator haunting southern Stonetalon Mountains. Posted on a roadside notice near Windshear Crag, the bounty directs adventurers into Sishir Canyon to claim the spider matriarch's fang for Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Putting an end to her reign makes the mountain roads safer for night travelers. Travelers along the main thoroughfare south of Windshear Crag will spot a weathered wanted poster warning of the dangers to the west. Sishir Canyon and Webwinder Path have been completely overrun by eight-legged predators. At the heart of this webbed menace sits Besseleth, an unusually large, orange-hued spider who commands her brood and ambushes anyone daring to stray off the path after sunset. The bounty on Besseleth is offered by Maggran Earthbinder, a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran has a personal score to settle with the matriarch: during a previous encounter, he was nearly killed when struck by Besseleth's massive two-foot fang. Though he managed to fight her off and limp to safety, the lingering wound serves as a constant reminder of the danger lurking in the canyon shadows. By having an adventurer claim Besseleth's Fang, Maggran hopes to secure the passes so trade and travel to Sun Rock Retreat can flourish without fear.

quest:629.text: The Vile Reef. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a piece of an ancient stone tablet resting deep beneath the Savage Coast. The sunken city, known as the Vile Reef, is infested with aggressive murlocs and holds the legendary history of Gri'lek, which the Darkspear tribe wishes to preserve in Orgrimmar. Northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp, an ancient troll city slipped beneath the waters along the Savage Coast when a violent earthquake shattered the land long ago. Now referred to as the Vile Reef, its flooded ruins crawl with hostile murlocs that assault anyone venturing near. Resting on the sea floor among the ruins is a massive stone tablet carved with the story of Gri'lek, a legendary troll hero whose memory remains sacred to the Darkspear. Because the full monument is far too massive to carry away from the depths, Kin'weelay asks you to break off a shard from the stone. He intends to carry this fragment back to Orgrimmar, enshrining it in a sacred place so the Darkspear will never forget the strength and honor of Gri'lek.

quest:635.text: Crystal in the Mountains. The Pendant of Myzrael pulses in your hand and a pleading reaches you, as if someone desperately needs help. A vision shows a gleaming crystal rising out of the ground in the northern mountains of Arathi, and you feel drawn to that place. The pendant pulses as you hold it. From it comes a sense of pleading, as if someone is trying to reach you and badly needs your help. Then a vision opens before you: the mountains in the north of Arathi, and a gleaming crystal thrusting up out of the ground. You feel drawn to that place.

quest:638.text: Trollbane. Vol'jin has ordered the Darkspear trolls to recover the ancient sword Trol'kalar from the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. With King Thoras Trollbane fallen, the blade is meant to serve the Horde in future conflicts against the trolls of Zul'Gurub. Following the death of King Thoras Trollbane and the collapse of Stromgarde into ruin, Chieftain Vol'jin has ordered that every effort be made to spirit Trol'kalar away. This storied blade has long rested in human hands, but the Darkspear tribe hopes to claim it for the battles looming against the jungle trolls dwelling within Zul'Gurub. To carry out Vol'jin's directive, a seasoned hunter named Zengu was sent to the Horde outpost of Hammerfall, situated in the northeastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands. Nimboya directs travelers from Stranglethorn Vale to seek out Zengu and assist in securing the legendary weapon.

quest:639.text: Sigil of Strom. Zengu in Hammerfall wants the sigils that guard Trol'kalar, the sword of Lord Ignaeus Trollbane. The first, the Sigil of Strom, was taken by the Syndicate, and a Syndicate agent in Stromgarde is likely to hold it. In ancient times the trolls fought the Arathorian Empire, and their ablest foe was Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane. He went into battle wielding Trol'kalar, a name that means troll slayer in the trolls' old tongue. Now Trollbane's sons are weakened and their stronghold lies in ruins. Several sigils protect the sword, and the survivors of Stromgarde each took a share of them. Zengu says they must all be retrieved. The Syndicate seized the first, and Zengu reckons one of their agents in Stromgarde has it. Bring it back to him at Hammerfall.

quest:6481.text: Earthen Arise. Deep within Boulderslide Ravine, the shaman Mor'rogal discovers a slumbering Earthen named Goggeroc sealed inside a Resonite cask. Fearing the raw destructive power an ancient being of stone could unleash upon Kalimdor, he sends a champion to shatter the cask and strike Goggeroc down before the creature can recover its full strength. While investigating the vermin infestation in Boulderslide Ravine, scouts discovered a strange relic nestled among the kobolds: a Resonite cask radiating unearthly force. Mor'rogal, a tauren shaman stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, recognized the container for what it truly was—a prison and sanctuary housing Goggeroc, a dormant Earthen. These primordial creations of stone possess strength that outmatches mortal warriors, making the prospect of Goggeroc roaming free an existential threat to the region.

quest:6547.text: Warsong Scout Update. Warsong Scout Update is a Horde communication task connecting the outpost commanders along the borders of Ashenvale with forward scouts watching the contested forest. Carrying strategic orders from Kadrak, couriers ensure the Warsong Clan maintains tight surveillance against ambushing night elves. It highlights the tenuous, hostile grip the Horde strives to maintain over their newly claimed territory. The borderlands of Ashenvale remain a powder keg where neither side yields an inch. Horde forces under Kadrak rely heavily on dispersed Warsong scouts stationed in high-risk outposts to track night elf movements and secure contested supply lines. Because the forest itself provides natural cover to the stealthy sentinels of the Alliance, regular reports and written updates are critical to keeping isolated scouts from being cut off and overwhelmed. For the Warsong clan, every stretch of forest cleared or occupied has been paid for in blood. The scouts watch constantly for retaliatory night elf raids aiming to reclaim the woodlands. Delivering Kadrak's orders reassures the vanguard that reinforcements and coordination remain active, allowing the scouts to report back that their defensive measures are succeeding despite continuous elven resistance.

quest:657.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Quae has gone through the folder and learned that Apothecary Jorell is running deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. Quae is in poor shape after clashing with orcs and cannot help Kinelory, who will need your protection when she heads for the farm to steal any of Jorell's research not yet sent to Tarren Mill. Quae reads through the folder and finds that Apothecary Jorell is running deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. How that touches Hillsbrad is unclear to Quae, yet Phin would not want it to go on. Some of Jorell's research has already been sent to Tarren Mill. While you were away, Quae clashed with some orcs and is in no shape to help Kinelory. Kinelory means to go down to the farm and steal the research Jorell has not yet sent to Tarren Mill, and she will need protection. You are to speak to Kinelory.

quest:658.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Quae and Kin have been watching Go'Shek Farm for days. Kin saw a courier come out of a small house to the south, and they suspect the courier carries notes bound for Tarren Mill. Quae wants those documents and asks whether you are a skilled tracker. Quae is not surprised that Phin Odelic sent you to check on them, since Phin worries too much. Quae and Kin have been watching the farm for days. Not long ago Kin saw a courier come out of a small house to the south. Kin talks a lot, but Quae can always trust Kin's senses in dangerous areas. Quae asks whether you are a skilled tracker. The courier may carry notes bound for Tarren Mill, and getting hold of those documents could shed some light on what is happening in Hillsbrad. You are to find the Forsaken Courier and bring her Sealed Folder back to Quae near Go'Shek Farm. While you search, Kin spots an apothecary leaving that same house. Quae is confident the apothecary is up to no good, but needs proof before anyone does something rash.

quest:659.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Phin Odelic leads a band of adventurers looking into odd happenings in the area, and believes the undead are involved. Two companions, Quae and Kinelory, headed for Go'Shek Farm, in the Arathi Highlands. No word has come from them for days. Not long ago, a cousin of Phin's in Hillsbrad had to put down his dog, Stanley. The beast had mystically swollen to a huge size and savagely turned on anyone who came near. Phin believes the undead are involved in the odd happenings, and the group is looking for signs to prove it. Quae and Kinelory, two of Phin's companions, headed into the Arathi Highlands, to Go'Shek Farm, and have not checked in for days. Phin grows concerned and wants you to find them near the farm.

quest:660.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is ready to head down to the farm and wants you at her side. She fears the undead may be doing harm back in Hillsbrad the longer they wait, and you are asked to see her safely back to Quae. After the earlier steps of the investigation, Kinelory is ready to act. She asks you to come with her down to the farm. You are to see her safely back to Quae, and anyone who cares about the people of Hillsbrad is urged to protect her.

quest:661.text: Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is back from the farm, none the worse for wear, and Quae has the items she brought. Quae and Kinelory mean to stay in Arathi a while longer, so it falls to you to carry word to Phin Odelic in Southshore. Quae is pleased with how well you looked after Kinelory, who has come back in better shape than after a night at the tavern. The items from the farm should give Phin Odelic some idea of what is happening out in Arathi. Since the farm was attacked, Quae and Kinelory plan to stay put a little longer in case of retaliation, and ask you to go back to Southshore and speak to Phin.

quest:663.text: Land Ho!. At Faldir's Cove, the lookout Lolo greets you with news that Captain O'Breen's stop here will last far longer than planned. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, are lost, and Lolo suggests you speak with the captain. Lolo, ever on the lookout, spots you arriving at Faldir's Cove. Captain O'Breen had promised the crew only a few hours here, time enough to collect the treasure and head back to Booty Bay. Lolo doubts it will be so quick. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, now rest on the bottom of the sea. Anyone who means to stay is told to talk to the captain.

quest:681.text: Northfold Manor. Captain Nials, at Refuge Pointe, asks for help against the Syndicate holding Northfold Manor. Their hold on the land between the defenders of Stromgarde and Southshore makes it hard for supplies to arrive. Stromgarde has been carved up between the ogres, the Syndicate and the Alliance, and every faction fights the others to a bloody stalemate. The Alliance's forces dwindle while their enemies grow. The defenders need help from Southshore, but supplies are slow to arrive. The Syndicate holds the ground between the defenders and Southshore. Captain Nials wants you to go to their base at Northfold Manor and cut down their highwaymen and mercenaries, in the hope that the pressure on the supply trains eases and more get through.

quest:691.text: Worth Its Weight in Gold. At Refuge Pointe, Apprentice Kryten is after Witherbark tusks, medicine pouches and a shadow hunter's knife, all reagents for Archmage Malin, who sent him and Skuerto to gather them. He asks you to seek them among the Witherbark trolls in the southeast of Arathi. Archmage Malin sent Kryten and Skuerto to Arathi to collect reagents, and Kryten had no idea how to gather them until you arrived. He needs ten Witherbark tusks, four medicine pouches and one shadow hunter knife. The Witherbark trolls make their home in the southeast of Arathi. By Kryten's research, any Witherbark troll should have tusks, and the witch doctors carry the medicine pouches. The knife belongs to the mightiest shadow hunters, handed to them after they finish their rites of passage. Only battle will show which of them has one.

quest:693.text: Wand over Fist. Skuerto at Refuge Pointe has worked out where the first of Trelane's items ended up. Kor'gresh has Trelane's Wand of Invocation in Boulderfist Hall, and Skuerto wants it brought back. After your work for Apprentice Kryten, Skuerto has found where Trelane's first item went. Kor'gresh holds it in Boulderfist Hall, and has been throwing blasts of ice at his own kin to keep them in line. Skuerto reckons the ogre must be close to figuring out all of the wand's powers. Boulderfist Hall lies south of Refuge Pointe and then east of Thandol Span.

quest:694.text: Trelane's Defenses. With the wand in hand, Skuerto turns to the ogres that surround the Tower of Arathor. To bring the tower's defenses to life, he needs an azure agate from the Boulderfist shaman, to be taken to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe. Ogres surround the Tower of Arathor in Stromgarde. Skuerto says the tower's defenses must be activated if you are to stand a chance against them and still reach the items alive. Certain gems from the tower have caught the fancy of the Boulderfist shaman, who carried them off, though Skuerto says they will not keep them for long. Bring one azure agate to Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, who knows the spell to enchant it so that it works as a key.

quest:695.text: An Apprentice's Enchantment. Apprentice Kryten has enchanted the agate you brought him from the Boulderfist shaman. Touched to a pedestal at the foot of the tower, it will wake the tower's defenses. Before you leave, he sends you to Skuerto for the rest. Kryten hands you the enchanted gem. He explains that touching it to a pedestal at the foot of the tower will wake the tower's defenses, and that you should use it when you are ready to go in after the rest of Trelane's items. He will await your return at the camp. First, speak to Skuerto, who will fill in whatever else you need to know.

quest:696.text: Attack on the Tower. With the tower's defenses awake, Skuerto at Refuge Pointe sends you into the ogre-held tower for Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. They should lie in chests inside, and Skuerto says Malin will be more than pleased if you bring them back. After Kryten's enchantment, Skuerto tells you what to look for: Trelane's phylactery, orb and ember agate. The three should be sitting in chests inside the tower, and you should have no trouble opening them yourself, though the ogres call for care. The tower's defenses will not deal with them on their own, and if the ogres find you stealing from them, they will put the hurt on you.

quest:697.text: Malin's Request. Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin, who is found in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It tells Malin that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon, and Skuerto is certain Malin will repay you well for helping them in Arathi. After the work in Arathi, Skuerto hands you a letter to take back to Stormwind. Its message for Archmage Malin in the Mage Quarter is that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto has no doubt that Malin will repay you well for helping them, and sends you off with a wish for a safe journey.

quest:702.text: Guile of the Raptor. After the earlier Guile of the Raptor, Tor'gan hands you an orb and sends you to Gor'mul at Hammerfall. Its energy carries the essence of the raptor, meant to stir Gor'mul's spirit and give him new purpose. Tor'gan gives you an orb whose energy is meant to fill Gor'mul with the raptor's essence. He hopes it will rouse the warrior's spirit and set him on a fresh course in life. Once Gor'mul is himself again, Tor'gan means to explain the current state of the Horde to him and gain a great warrior's help in the unceasing battles. Gor'mul greets your return with sourness, saying he wants nothing more than more of Tor'gan's pity and mocking you with talk of brightly colored string.

quest:731.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. Deep in the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel refuses to abandon his dig site without a prize to show the Explorers' League. Despite his severe forgetfulness and an infestation of hostile troggs, he insists on uncovering a mysterious fossil before retreating. Ensuring the dwarven researcher survives his erratic search allows word of his safety to reach his assistant back in Auberdine. Remtravel's Dig lies far to the south of Darkshore, nestled among ancient ruins that were supposed to hold forgotten secrets. Instead, the dwarven excavators struck into pockets of savage troggs, driving out the workers and leaving the camp under siege. While most would flee for Auberdine immediately, Prospector Remtravel became fixated on salvaging his findings. Refusing to leave empty-handed, he wanders right into the teeth of danger to recover an elusive fossil to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

quest:741.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. This errand delivers a strange petrified specimen recovered from the wild beaches of Darkshore to the Explorers' League outpost in Darnassus. Archaeologist Hollee refuses to abandon her distracted colleague in the field, entrusting the specimen's transport to a passing adventurer instead. The fossil's arrival in the night elven capital immediately captures the keen interest of Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Prospector Remtravel's excavations along the misty coast of Darkshore have unearthed a curious fossil, but digging deeper matters more to him than protocol. Archaeologist Hollee, unwilling to leave the wandering prospector alone amidst the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists, remains behind to watch over him. In order to get the discovery documented, she requires an Alliance traveler to ferry the specimen up to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild maintains a scholarly delegation. Dwarves from Ironforge have crossed the Great Sea in force under the banner of the Explorers' League, eager to unearth ancient relics and lost history beneath the soil of Kalimdor. Receiving the artifact in the elven capital, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker wastes no time in marveling over Remtravel's knack for uncovering ancient treasures. While night elves view their forests as living sanctuaries, the League views the ancient lands as an expansive archaeological dig waiting to be deciphered.

quest:742.text: The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a summons dispatched to young Horde champions visiting Thunder Bluff, urging them north into the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Delivered by the city's heralds, the call directs travelers to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to take part in a proving hunt. Within the serene heights of Thunder Bluff, runners keep the burgeoning Horde informed of opportunities beyond the borders of Mulgore. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation aimed at proven adventurers looking for greater challenges. With the Horde establishing footholds deep in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, young warriors are called upon to bolster those outposts and test their survival skills in a far harsher environment. Ashenvale represents both rich resources and severe peril for the Horde. Two prominent encampments anchor the faction's presence in the territory: Splintertree Post along the main road, and a remote outpost perched upon the western coast at Zoram Strand. Arriving at Splintertree Post puts incoming recruits directly under the wing of Senani Thunderheart, a veteran outdoorswoman organizing a massive hunt designed to tame the wilderness and claim glory for the Horde.

quest:847.text: Guile of the Raptor. After Tor'gan's orb gave Gor'mul the raptor's essence, the power he felt has him wondering about the shamans' magic. He sends you to tell Tor'gan he has been convinced, for the time being, and will listen. Gor'mul wonders aloud whether the power coursing through him is the shamans' power that Tor'gan tried to show him. He finds it interesting. He asks you to tell Tor'gan that he has been convinced, for the time being, and will hear what Tor'gan has to say.

quest:876.text: Serena Bloodfeather. This bounty task charges Horde adventurers with slaying Serena Bloodfeather, the matriarch driving harpy raids against Crossroads supply lines. Her campaign is a personal blood feud stemming from the Champion of the Horde Rexxar slaying her sister. Putting an end to Serena aims to shatter the coordination behind the harpy flock in the northern Barrens. The Witchwing harpies infesting the crags northwest of the Crossroads do not strike solely out of animalistic hunger. Their leader, Serena Bloodfeather, wages an explicit blood feud against the Horde. Years ago during the founding of Durotar, the wandering beastmaster Rexxar struck down Serena's sister, a notorious matriarch named Bloodfeather. Consumed by hatred for the nascent Horde, Serena has rallied her flock into an organized scourge intent on butchering supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

quest:878.text: Tribes at War. Tribes at War is a Horde quest offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. Trapped behind bars by the tauren, Mangletooth barters critical intelligence about quilboar incursions in exchange for the slaughter of rival Bristleback spiritual leaders. Caged in Camp Taurajo, the Razormane quilboar Mangletooth proves that captivity does not blunt old hatreds. The Barrens has long been contested between two dominant quilboar factions: the Razormane and the Bristleback. While the Horde struggles to secure its settlements and supply lines against sudden ambushes, Mangletooth offers valuable insight into who is truly tormenting Thork's outpost—provided a champion of the Horde first cuts down the Bristleback's most revered casters. Mangletooth directs adventurers north against the Bristleback's mystical core: their Water Seekers, Thornweavers, and Geomancers. Both tribes revere the earth and draw raw power from ancient magic tied to their demigod progenitor, Agamaggan. By eliminating their casters, the Horde strikes a crippling blow to Bristleback ritual strength, leaving them vulnerable to Razormane rivals and reducing pressure on nearby trails.

quest:889.text: Spirit of the Wind. Spirit of the Wind is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By channeling the residual power within Agamaggan's blood shards, Mangletooth infuses travelers with swiftness to outpace the vast savannas of the Barrens. In the arid sprawl of the Barrens, crossing open territory quickly can mean the difference between survival and falling to predatory beasts or wandering centaur warbands. The captive quilboar Mangletooth, imprisoned within Camp Taurajo, understands the latent power sleeping within the red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. When handed ten of these relics, he draws upon their primeval resonance to bestow the Spirit of the Wind, granting travelers a burst of fleet-footed momentum to outrun the howling drafts of the plains. Quilboar tradition reveres Agamaggan, the Great Boar who shed his blood across central Kalimdor during the ancient War of the Ancients. Even in captivity, Mangletooth retains intimate knowledge of the wild god's rites. Channelling the god's spilled blood does not merely alter the flesh; it stirs wild vigor, allowing a runner to match the velocity of the galloping zhevra herds. Though the quilboar are bitter enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth remains willing to impart Agamaggan's boons to anyone willing to fuel his rituals with fresh shards.

quest:89.text: The Everstill Bridge. The Everstill Bridge is a rebuilding effort led by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire to repair the town's damaged stone bridge. Progress has ground to a halt because iron meant for the project was redirected into weapons during the last orc invasion, and the replacement caravan from Stormwind was ambushed by Redridge gnolls. The stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, connecting the western roads back toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. During the recent orc incursions, the town was pushed to the brink. With survival hanging in the balance, Lakeshire melted down its structural iron supplies to forge munitions, blades, and plate armor to repel the Blackrock invaders, leaving the bridge incomplete and vulnerable. Foreman Oslow petitioned the House of Nobles and Stormwind for fresh construction materials to finish repairs. A supply caravan laden with iron was dispatched, but it never arrived. A warband of Redridge gnolls ambushed the convoy along the road, carting away vital iron pikes and rivets into their camps in the northern hills. Without adventurous travelers willing to reclaim the stolen hardware, the bridge project remains stalled while gnolls and orcs tighten their grip on the mountains.

quest:891.text: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet has had enough of his merchant vessels being blasted to splinters by the Alliance gunners at Northwatch Hold. He hires Horde champions to march down the Merchant Coast, silence the hold's artillery officers, and take the badges of their fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold looms over the southern coast of the Barrens, established as a fortified bastion for the humans of Theramore. While intended to guard Alliance interests and monitor Horde activity in Kalimdor, the soldiers within have succumbed to severe paranoia. Viewing any unfamiliar sail as hostile, their rampart batteries open fire indiscriminately, threatening peaceful merchant traffic and the privateering vessels of Ratchet. Captain Brightsun refuses to let his ships be sunk without consequence. The strike against Northwatch targets its command: Captain Fairmount and her chief cannoneers, Whessan and Smythe. Striking them down and stripping Theramore medals from the garrison's soldiers leaves the hold's artillery disarrayed, granting Ratchet's maritime operations breathing room along the Merchant Coast.

quest:898.text: Free From the Hold. Free From the Hold is an escort quest in the Barrens where Horde adventurers rescue Gilthares Firebough from human captors at Northwatch Hold. Captured after his transport was intercepted and sunk, the elf deckhand seeks a daring break out to reunite with his captain in Ratchet. Northwatch Hold stands as Theramore's military spearhead on the Barrens coast, vigilant and aggressive toward any perceived threat. That paranoia caught Gilthares Firebough in its net. His ship, running moonshine along the commercial lane between Ratchet and Booty Bay, was bombarded and sent to the ocean floor by Alliance forces. As the lone survivor plucked from the wreckage, Gilthares was thrown into Northwatch's dungeons accused of being an enemy agent conspiring against the Alliance. Despite his jailers painting him as a dangerous saboteur, Gilthares insists he is nothing more than a humble deckhand caught carrying illicit liquor. With the aid of Horde forces willing to strike at Northwatch, he makes a desperate bid for freedom, fighting his way out of the fortress and fleeing north up the shoreline to Ratchet. There, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun welcomes the returned crewmate back into the fold of the Thalo'dan Privateers.

quest:899.text: Consumed by Hatred. Consumed by Hatred is a grim task given by Mankrik at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Tormented by the violent ambush that separated him from his wife, the grieving orc directs his agonizing uncertainty into a relentless vendetta against the Bristleback quilboar. He calls upon Horde travelers to slaughter the creatures in droves and return with a massive tally of their tusks. Standing under the harsh sun of the Crossroads, Mankrik is a warrior possessed by grief. After surviving a vicious raid by the quilboar that left him battered and his wife missing, he spends his waking hours watching the arid horizon for any sign of the pig men. His thirst for their blood remains unquenched despite the many he has personally cut down, driving him to seek help from fellow members of the Horde. Rather than seeking peace or solace, Mankrik demands trophies of raw slaughter: sixty Bristleback quilboar tusks. To him, each shattered tusk represents a measure of suffering returned upon the monsters that tore his life apart. While piles of bone cannot heal his grief or quell his desire for retribution, seeing the Bristlebacks bleed brings a fleeting, bitter satisfaction to the wounded warrior.

quest:913.text: Cry of the Thunderhawk. Cry of the Thunderhawk is the culmination of Jorn Skyseer's hunting trials in the southern Barrens. Entrusted by the elders at Camp Taurajo, a hunter must seek out a winged serpent soaring through the scrublands and bring back its wings to prove their mastery over the savanna's fiercest beasts. After proving their mettle against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, hunters in the Barrens are directed toward their ultimate challenge by Jorn Skyseer. The thunderhawk is considered one of the most fierce aerial predators inhabiting the scrublands surrounding Camp Taurajo. Slaying one requires patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess. Returning with the thunderhawk's wings marks the end of a novice's tutelage under Camp Taurajo's watchful eyes. For the tauren, hunting is not mere slaughter but an ongoing spiritual walk in harmony with the Earthmother and the natural hierarchy of the wild. Besting such a proud creature shows that the hunter acts with strength, courage, and honor—virtues required before stepping out into harsher wildernesses beyond the central plains.

quest:92706.text: WANTED: Bruuz. WANTED: Bruuz is a bounty posted by Gazlowe in the goblin port of Ratchet. A massive predatory shark has taken up residence near the harbor docks, threatening maritime traffic and coastal trade until someone puts an end to it. Ratchet thrives on merchant shipping, serving as the primary neutral gateway between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. That steady stream of commerce makes the waters around the docks bustling and chaotic, but recently it has drawn a far more dangerous visitor. A gargantuan shark, dubbed 'Bruuz' by the frightened dockworkers, has begun prowling the bay. Rather than remaining in deep water, the beast aggressively targets small skiffs, local sailors, and offloading cargo, disrupting port operations. Gazlowe cannot afford to have vessels avoiding his port out of fear of getting mauled by sea life. So he has posted a public bounty notice calling on all anglers and promising a hefty reward. To claim it, a hunter must slay Bruuz and haul back the predator's dorsal fin as proof of the deed.

quest:93.text: Dusky Crab Cakes. Chef Grual of Darkshire's Scarlet Raven Tavern has a secret behind his famous Dusky Crab Cakes: they contain no crab at all. Tasked with aiding the famished and nervous Jitters, adventurers are sent to harvest spider legs from the deadly arachnids roaming northern Duskwood to prepare the town's beloved snack. Duskwood has long suffered from isolation, dark magic, and severed supply routes, forcing the locals of Darkshire to adapt their cuisine. Chef Grual, the resident cook at the Scarlet Raven Tavern, solved his meat shortages by inventing the Dusky Crab Cake. Despite the name suggesting seafood from distant shores, Grual readily admits that the dish's distinctively tangy flavor comes entirely from the gooey legs of local giant spiders. To fulfill the order, Grual directs hunters north toward the foothills and riverbanks where Venom Web Spiders spin their snares. In a gloomy forest crawling with undead and feral beasts, harvesting fresh spider meat is hazardous work, yet it remains one of the few readily available protein sources in the blighted woods. Grual fries the seasoned arachnid limbs on a hot skillet until they skitter to a crisp.

quest:94.text: A Watchful Eye. A Watchful Eye is an Alliance quest issued by the wizard Theocritus from the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest. Having established a basic scrying link against his rival Morganth, Theocritus directs adventurers east into Redridge Mountains to plant an enchanted focus upon an ancient lion statue watching the Tower of Ilgalar. From his tower in eastern Elwynn Forest, the mage Theocritus maintains a vigilant watch over dark spellcraft brewing in the nearby hills. His chief nemesis is Morganth, a vicious sorcerer of formidable power who has claimed the Tower of Ilgalar in the crags of Redridge Mountains. Seeking to uncover Morganth's sinister ambitions before they spill across the border, Theocritus developed the Eye of Azora to surveil the rogue wizard from a distance. While visual scrying affords some information, it is not enough to divine Morganth's deeper schemes. Theocritus entrusts travelers with the Glyph of Azora, commanding them to trek to the shadow of the Tower of Ilgalar. There, keeping a lonely watch for decades, stands an Old Lion Statue. Setting the glyph into a worn depression at the statue's base awakens an arcane conduit, linking the stone back to Azora and allowing Theocritus to delve straight into his rival's mind.

quest:942.text: The Absent Minded Prospector. This quest bridges an excavation mystery from Darkshore across the Great Sea to the Wetlands. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker entrusts you with a strange Kalimdor fossil, directing you to Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor to unlock its secrets. While examining the strange fossil uncovered in Darkshore, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker notices a striking resemblance to a relic shown at an Explorers' League conference back in Ironforge. That earlier piece was presented by Archaeologist Flagongut, who was convinced that such fossils held latent powers waiting to be unlocked. Greywhisker believes Flagongut is the only dwarf capable of discerning what makes this Kalimdor find so extraordinary. Carrying the mysterious relic means undertaking a long journey out of Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Flagongut was last seen waiting for an armed escort to the Whelgar Excavation Site while lodging at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Delivering the fossil into his hands marks the turning point where a local Darkshore survey ties into a continent-spanning archaeological inquiry.

quest:951.text: Mathystra Relics. This quest sends Alliance adventurers north along the coast of Darkshore to sift through the overgrown Ruins of Mathystra. Onu, an Ancient of Lore rooted in the Grove of the Ancients, seeks these ancient kaldorei artifacts to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cult is manipulating night elven sorcery for their sinister rites. To counteract this dark endeavor, Onu directs heroes to the Ruins of Mathystra, located along the northeastern shores of Darkshore. Long ago, Mathystra was a shining bastion of highborne civilization before it shattered during the Sundering. Though the city has collapsed into rubble, weeds, and naga infestation, powerful remnants of its original arcane and spiritual enchantments linger in shattered urns and ancient relics scattered across the stone foundations.

quest:970.text: The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks a critical turn in the investigation of the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand, shifting the pursuit from the ruined Tower of Althalaxx in Darkshore across the border to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier dispatches adventurers into nearby cultist camps to secure a potent Glowing Soul Gem. Unlocking this artifact reveals the grim sorcery that fuels the cult's influence over the northern forests. After uncovering the ominous activities around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, reports led directly south into Ashenvale to Delgren the Purifier. Stationed at Maestra's Post, Delgren has long contended with the Cult of the Dark Strand encroaching on the ancient elven woods. Recognizing that the cult's threat spans across both territories, Delgren resolves to strike at the heart of their vile sorcery. Northeast of Maestra's Post lies the ruins of Ordil'Aran, now overrun by fanatical Dark Strand cultists. Delgren identifies that their operatives carry glowing soul gems—dark vessels enchanted with sinister magic that sustain the cult's power. By hunting down the cultists among the ruins and reclaiming one of these gems, Delgren intends to shatter their enchantment and expose the true source behind their malevolent rite.

quest:972.text: Water Sapta. Water Sapta is a transitional task bestowed upon young Horde shaman by Islen Waterseer along the coast of the Barrens. Imbued with a ritual brew, the shaman is sent across the Great Sea to the blighted lands of Silverpine Forest to face a corrupted spring. In the elemental traditions of the Horde's shaman, a sapta is an alchemical draught crafted to attune the senses directly to the spirits of the world. While common eyes perceive only tranquil streams or stagnant ponds, drinking a sapta pierces the veil of the physical plane, revealing the elemental beings dwelling within the current. Having demonstrated their dedication to the spirits, the shaman receives the concoction directly from Islen Waterseer, a hermit dwelling along the desolate shores south of Ratchet. Rather than testing the sapta in the arid valleys of Kalimdor, Islen commands the initiate to journey far across the Great Sea to the shadowy, forsaken woods of Silverpine Forest to confront an elemental corruption poisoning Lordaeron's streams.

quest:98071.text: Brewer's Trade. A trade has been worked out with the Dun Garok brew-kin, who miss the Fallrook family's vineyards as much as anyone. A case of Fallrook Varietal travels to their fort in the southeast of Hillsbrad Foothills, and a sack of their Homebrew Hops comes back. Most of the best bottled years of Fallrook wine are long since drunk, but cases of the Fallrook Varietal still sit in the cellars. The Dun Garok brew-kin miss the vineyards of the Fallrook family too, and a trade has been worked out with them. The case goes southeast to Dun Garok, to be left with the brew-kin beside the fireplace where they gather, down at the base of their fort. In return, you carry a sack of their Homebrew Hops back.

quest:98362.text: To Thunder Bluff. To Thunder Bluff marks the triumphant return of a young tauren druid from their communion with the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Having earned the favor of the Great Cat Spirit, the initiate returns to Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise to master the art of feline shapeshifting. After proving their insight and worth before Dendrite Starblaze and the Great Cat Spirit in the sacred groves of Moonglade, a young druid must carry the spirit's blessings back to Mulgore. The communion with such primal powers represents a pivotal milestone in a druid's training, bridging ancient night elven teachings with the tauren's own earthen heritage. Awaiting your return high atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff is Turak Runetotem. While Dendrite facilitated communion with the spirit itself, it falls to Turak to guide the physical transformation. With the blessing of the Great Cat Spirit acknowledged, the elder trainer imparts the sacred knowledge required to adopt the swift, predatory shape of the cat.

quest:98397.text: To Darnassus. To Darnassus is the culmination of a night elf druid's journey to commune with the Great Cat Spirit. After proving yourself to Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, you are sent back to the Cenarion Enclave to master the art of shifting into cat form. Having commune with the Great Cat Spirit through the guidance of Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, an aspiring night elf druid must return to Teldrassil. Starblaze acknowledges that you have proven yourself a worthy student and directs you back to your primary instructor, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, waiting beneath the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Upon arriving in Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker acknowledges that you have absorbed the wisdom of the Great Cat Spirit. In his eyes, every generation of druids faces a trial shaped by this ancient entity, which is as playful as it is deadly. With your connection established and your spirit prepared, Mathrengyl imparts the final rites necessary to shift into the graceful form of the cat.

quest:98463.text: Talk of the Town. A friendly barkeep points travelers eager for a livelier gathering toward the port of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Those looking for wilder company are directed to seek out Nixxrax Fillamug at the Salty Sailor Tavern. Word passes quickly between drink-servers and their patrons, and news travels far beyond the local counter. A friendly bartender passes along a tip about where the genuine commotion is brewing, pointing anyone searching for wilder spectacles toward the port of Booty Bay. The destination is the Salty Sailor Tavern, a lively establishment maintained by goblins amidst the bustle of Stranglethorn Vale. There, Nixxrax Fillamug keeps cups topped up for anyone who walks in.

quest:986.text: A Lost Master. A Lost Master tasks an Alliance adventurer with gathering materials to aid in the search for Volcor, a night elf lost in the wilderness of Darkshore. Terenthis in Auberdine offers to weave an enchanted camouflage cloak to protect the rescuer, requiring pelts from the coast's fiercest moonstalkers. While tracking threats along the coast of Darkshore, Terenthis in Auberdine becomes concerned for the fate of Volcor and his companion, Grimclaw. Venturing deep into the southern reaches of the region is notoriously dangerous due to aggressive predators and corrupted wildlife. Rather than sending a scout unprotected, Terenthis devises a plan to craft a protective cloak imbued with wild illusions. To weave a cloak capable of confounding Darkshore's beasts, standard hides are insufficient. Terenthis requires fine moonstalker pelts taken specifically from mature moonstalker sires or matriarchs. These formidable great cats prowl the woodlands south of Auberdine near the Wildbend River and extend toward the forested border of Ashenvale. The finished garment uses moonstalker fur and nature enchantments to let the wearer pass unhindered through hostile territory while searching for Volcor. However, Terenthis warns that the illusion is delicate: engaging in strenuous activity or combat breaks the enchantment, leaving the searcher exposed.

quest:993.text: A Lost Master. Having gathered fine moonstalker pelts, you carry the completed Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak into the wilds of Darkshore to find the missing night elf, Volcor. Guided by his loyal white bear Grimclaw, you must track down the wounded scout before hostile furbolgs finish him off. After Terenthis in Auberdine weaves the Enchanted Moonstalker Cloak, the search for the missing scout Volcor begins in earnest. His bear companion, Grimclaw, has returned to the road south of the settlement, standing watch for any ally sent by Terenthis. By offering a familiar greeting to the loyal beast, travelers are led directly off the beaten track toward the cave where Volcor lies in hiding.

quest:995.text: Escape Through Stealth. Escape Through Stealth is an Alliance escort quest set in Darkshore. After locating the trapped night elf scout Volcor deep within a furbolg den, the player helps guide him safely past hostile beasts to freedom before reporting back to Terenthis in Auberdine. Volcor, an operative sent into the depths of Darkshore to investigate the region's mounting threats, ended up cornered inside a furbolg cave. Outnumbered and cut off from the main roads, he relies on a passing ally to coordinate an exit before the hostile furbolgs realize he is slipping away. Rather than attempting a suicidal frontal charge, Volcor chooses caution. Relying on shadows and deliberate maneuvering, he slips past the corrupted denizens of the cavern. Knowing that speed and quiet are paramount, Volcor separates from his rescuer once outside the mouth of the cave, racing ahead on foot while instructing his savior to meet him at the settlement of Auberdine. Upon returning to Auberdine, the player delivers news of the rescue to Terenthis, a night elf leader coordinating efforts to protect the troubled coastline. Terenthis views Volcor's safe return as proof that the encroaching darkness throughout Darkshore and the wilderness beyond can be resisted with discipline and teamwork.
